articleTitle: Implementation of Artificial Intelligence as a Disruptive Innovation Trend in the Postal Services Sector
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: In today's postal sector, automation is gaining more and more ground making human labour redundant. Although lagging behind in this indicator, the Bulgarian postal sector is starting to introduce automated postal stations (APS) in increasing numbers. This study aims to present the implementation of artificial intelligence and other digital technologies in APS as a disruptive innovation, and the implications of this trend for the Postal services sector. In this regard, fundamental issues are addressed: which business processes in the Postal Services Sector could be affected by digital disruptive innovations; to what extent are they likely to be affected; and what are the most threatened Postal services business processes in the near future. Some conclusions are drawn on this basis.

articleTitle: Investigating the Possibilities of Infrared Thermography for the Detection of Hoof Problems in Dairy Cows
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The aim of the study was to investigate the possibility of using infrared thermography to detect hoof problems in dairy cows. Cows were visually diagnosed by a veterinarian, after which thermographic images were taken of cows with inflamed hooves and those with healthy ones as well. Surface temperatures were obtained by specialized software and calculations were made. The results showed that, under certain conditions, infrared thermography can be used as an aid in the detection of hoof problems, but in order to refine this technique and increase its effectiveness, further research needs to be done.

articleTitle: The Potential of Agrophotovoltaics in Sustainable Energy Generation: A Case Study in Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Bangladesh, with its extensive agricultural landscape, faces considerable energy shortages. Adopting a dual-use strategy for agricultural land, which combines solar technology for energy generation and agricultural practices, could be highly advantageous in the future. To this end, this paper proposes a systematic approach to evaluate the feasibility of APV through proper modeling, design and analysis in a fertile land. The proposed methodology focuses on Naogaon in Bangladesh's Rajshahi division, assessing the viability of Agrophotovoltaic (APV) systems. AquaCrop is used for crop yield analysis, and HelioScope for solar plant design and power generation. Results show the Levelized Cost of Electricity (LCOE) for the APV system to be economically favorable at $0.0358, with an annual electricity output of 57.33 MWh. Furthermore, the APV system enables agricultural productivity, yielding 3.73 tons of crops per hectare. Environmental benefits are substantial, including a 30-ton annual reduction in greenhouse gas emissions. The study also calculates a significant Social Cost of Carbon (SCC) at $45,750, demonstrating the system's effectiveness in carbon emission reduction. This research offers a critical framework for future APV system implementations, especially in countries where agriculture is a key economic and environmental element, representing an important stride towards sustainable and renewable energy solutions.

articleTitle: Reverification of the Alkaline Hot Springs Efficacy on Arteriosclerosis using Changes in Skin Cholesterol Levels due to Mid-infrared Light Absorption Spectrum: based on Improved Analytical Methods and the Mathematical Model of Arteriosclerosis Development
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The efficacy of Yuda Onsen (Japan) for arteriosclerosis was tried to be reverified based on the change of the difference between the "peak" and "valley" of the absorption spectrum of cholesterol ester after bathing. The measurement principle of cholesterol ester is to irradiate the skin with light in the mid-infrared region and determine the cholesterol ester level of the skin from the absorption spectrum intensity. As a result of reverification of efficacy of Yuda Onsen against arteriosclerosis, the improved analysis method found that alkaline hot springs may have an efficacy on arteriosclerosis because bathing in alkaline springs contribute to the decrease in cholesterol levels.

articleTitle: Drone Sensor Units Applied in the Precision Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The challenging tasks of the precision agriculture require an extended study of novel equipment and comprehensive selection of particular sensors and sensor systems. Drones are powered by batteries which makes them sensitive in terms of energy consumption issues. A delicate balance must be ensured between functionality, price, size, weight and power supply of the device and its pickup equipment. In this regard they are designed and manufactured for specific applications. This study focuses on sensors and sensor systems used in the drone supplementary equipment for the purposes of the precision agriculture and remote monitoring systems, in particular. These are mainly sensors for distance and position, sensors for flight speed and image sensors.

articleTitle: ConvNeXt Based Deep Neural Network Model for Detection of Deepfake Speech
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Deepfake speech, generated by artificial intelligence or through the manipulation of existing speech recordings, raises serious concerns in areas such as privacy, social security, identity verification, and media integrity, posing an increasingly significant threat. Therefore, the development of speech-based deepfake detection and classification models is of paramount importance. This study employs a hybrid approach that integrates the ConvNeXt-Tiny model with machine learning-based techniques to identify and detect deepfake speech. The pre-trained ConvNeXt-Tiny model, which demonstrates effective performance in balancing detection accuracy and speed, is applied to speech samples obtained from the Fake-or-Real dataset, and deep features are extracted. The extracted deep features are then transferred to Extreme Learning Machine (ELM), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and Deep Neural Network (DNN) models. Experimental results show that the hybrid structure of ConvNeXt-Tiny deep features based on transfer learning and DNN achieves an accuracy of 96.64%, an F1-score of 96.63%, and a Cohen’s Kappa value of 0.893, outperforming other models. The proposed framework presents a model with accuracy comparable to state-of-the-art methods for detecting scenarios where an adversary transmits deepfake speech through channels such as phone calls, voice messages, or similar audio communication methods.

articleTitle: Chaotic Masking via Synchronization System based on Combined Type of Synchronization and Novel Hyperchaotic Model
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This paper presents a synthesis and application of a hyperchaotic synchronization system for secure communication using chaotic masking. Synchronization scheme between two identical novel mathematical models of a fourth-order hyperchaotic systems, is designed. The chosen type of synchronization combines projective, marginal and hybrid chaotic synchronizations. Active control is synthesized, based on the second Lyapunov stability law. The synchronization scheme is studied in Simulink environment, and the graphical results are displayed using MATLAB. This approach enhances the security and efficiency of data transmission, as sensitive information is concealed within a chaotic signal, making unauthorized decoding challenging. The main functional dependencies and the obtained graphical representations demonstrate that this combined synchronization method, when integrated with a hyperchaotic system, provides an effective and robust encryption solution that withstands some noise interferences, ensuring secure, efficient data transmission across open communication channels.

articleTitle: Using Large Language Models for Students’ Essays Plagiarism Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Large language models are used and fine-tuned today for different tasks. In educational environment, one problematic usage of this technology is for creation of plagiarism work. The focus of this work is to use large language models to detect plagiarised student essays. The recent relevant Kaggle competition "Detect AI Generated Text" is analysed. The top most accurate solutions in this competition used the ensembles of various large language models. In the efficiency track of the competition, winning solutions used more classical machine learning methods. We also analyse the main datasets used to finetune the LLM and machine learning models for students’ essays plagiarism detection. The most accurate models use comprehensive set of essay data and ensemble of different large language models.

articleTitle: Model of Digital to Analog Converter using Succesive Aproximation Register
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The article discusses about a design of an analog-to-digital converter with a successive approximation register. In the article, we described the basic internal blocks of the aforementioned AD converter. We emphasized the register of successive approximation. We verified the proposed AD converter by simulation and subsequently also verified it experimentally.

articleTitle: Synergistic Use of Offshore Wind, Wave, and Photovoltaics for Maritime Hydrogen Refueling: How the Synergy Impacts the Storage Requirements?
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This paper investigates the combined use of offshore wind, wave energy, and solar photovoltaics for maritime hydrogen refueling stations, with a focus on their influence on storage requirements. Eastern Crete and the Galite Islands, two Mediterranean sites with significant wind, wave, and solar energy potential, were selected as case studies for the installation of such stations. The research utilizes a Storage-to-Production Ratio (SPR) index to measure the amount of storage required to ensure a stable, uninterrupted hydrogen supply throughout the year, relative to the total annual hydrogen production. The results demonstrate that integrating either wind or wave energy with solar power significantly reduces the SPR, thanks to the weak temporal correlation between solar and the other two sources. This reduction can reach up to 20%, which, for a station providing an annual hydrogen supply of 20,000 tons, translates to a 4,000-ton reduction in storage needs. Conversely, combining wind and wave energy in the Mediterranean does not achieve a similar SPR reduction due to their strong temporal correlation.

articleTitle: Testing the Serial Data Streaming Feature of Microsoft Excel using an Angle Control System
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: In the paper, a method to achieve a hardware-software control system is presented, it could be an example for other control algorithms developing as well as an alternative to high-cost control implementation, especially in the research area. The hardware side consists of two ESP32 for high-speed and real-time wireless data exchange and an Arduino Due as USB interface with the PC. The angle value is acquired from a six-axis gyro-accelerometer sensor and send to the control algorithm implemented in Excel, which provides the command value to control the angular position. Wireless data transmission at high-speed is accomplished using ESP-NOW protocol designed by Espressif, and the serial communication between Arduino DUE and Excel is facilitated by Data Streamer a Microsoft developed add tool. Tests performed on the simulated drone arm show interesting characteristics that can be obtained if control technics are implemented in common software as Excel, also defining a low-cost method possible to be widely used in the future researches.

Author Keywords: high-speed and real-time wireless data exchange

articleTitle: Development of System using Computer Vision to Detect Personal Protective Equipment Violations
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This paper introduces a sophisticated computer vision system designed to improve industrial safety by automating the detection of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) violations. Utilizing the YOLOv8 algorithm, our system not only identifies the absence of essential safety equipment, such as helmets and jackets but also assesses compliance with safety protocols in real-time. The system was rigorously tested across various industrial settings, demonstrating high efficacy with enhanced mean average precision (mAP) compared to existing models. By integrating this system into current safety monitoring frameworks, we offer a dynamic solution that significantly boosts PPE adherence, potentially reducing workplace injuries and aligning with global safety standards.

articleTitle: MS Excel-based Implementation of Schmidt-Samoa Cryptosystems
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This paper describes the working principle of a Schmidt-Samoa cryptosystem, examining in detail the three main stages – key generation, encryption, and decryption. The most difficult points in the three stages are pointed out, with guidance given for dealing with the elusive problems – for example, determining the modular multiplicative inverse of an integer, as well as doing exponentiation when using large numbers, applying the "Square and Multiply" approach. An MS Excel implementation of the Schmidt-Samoa cryptosystem is described, which allows a very visual tabular representation of the three stages. Each of the three modules is explained in detail through a specific example. Numerous examples of encryption and decryption with the developed application are given, which find application in the educational process of the course "Telecommunication Security" for bachelor students of the "Internet and Mobile Communications" specialty at the University of Ruse.

articleTitle: Exploring the Integration of 74xx Library in Digital Circuit Design: A Case Study on Two-Bit Combinational Adder Synthesis and Analysis using Logisim Evolution
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This paper presents the theoretical foundations of half-adders, full one-bit adders, and multi-bit combinational adders, unraveling the complexities of their synthesis and implementation using integrated circuits. By delving into the intricacies of these fundamental building blocks of digital circuits, students will gain a comprehensive understanding of how these devices operate and interact within larger systems. Through a step-by-step guide, students will learn how to design and simulate two-bit combinational adders using Logisim Evolution, a powerful and intuitive digital logic simulator. The exploration of synthesis and implementation using integrated circuits, along with simulation techniques, offers invaluable benefits to students studying digital circuit design. By engaging in hands-on activities involving integrated circuits, students can bridge the gap between theoretical concepts and practical applications, enhancing their understanding of digital circuitry. The use of simulation tools such as Logisim Evolution provides a dynamic learning environment where students can visualize, experiment, and troubleshoot digital circuits in real time, reinforcing their comprehension and problem-solving skills. This experiential approach not only cultivates a deeper appreciation for the intricacies of digital logic but also equips students with essential skills for future endeavors in the field of digital circuit design.

articleTitle: YOLOv3 Tiny-Based Human Detection and Tracking using Vitis AI and VVAS on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Real-time human detection systems have become increasingly popular due to advancements in science and technology. Numerous studies have been conducted to enhance object recognition capabilities with higher accuracy and faster processing speeds. However, current methods still face several limitations, particularly in balancing the accuracy and processing speed of recognition algorithms. One of the current approaches is to deploy Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) on Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGA) to improve performance. Previous studies have achieved certain results in using FPGAs, but they often require deep knowledge of hardware design, which presents challenges for practical implementation. To address this issue, this paper introduces the use of VVAS (Vitis Video Analytics SDK) and Vitis AI to implement CNNs on FPGA without the need for deep intervention in hardware design. We employ the YOLOv3-Tiny (You Only Look Once) model to detect humans in real-time on the Kria KV260 Kit. Experimental results show that the system can process and recognize objects with high accuracy while ensuring fast processing speeds for applications in real-world surveillance environments.

articleTitle: A Critical Review of the New APQP Reference Manual for Automotive Quality Management
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The third edition of the Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP) Reference Manual was published by AIAG in March 2024. It is a good opportunity for organizations in the automotive industry to update their quality core tools and apply the new APQP elements to improve product quality. This paper focuses on the main differences and proposes ways to integrate the new APQP elements into the existing automotive quality management systems based on IATF 16949.

articleTitle: Latency and Link Speed for Service Robot Control over Mobile Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Designing and implementing a control system for a mobile service robot that operates in remote and harsh environments requires low latency and a reliable communication system. Current generation mobile networks such as 4G and 5G can be a perfect solution for achieving this goal. Thus, studying and developing mobile communication systems is a crucial milestone in the real-time two-way human-robot interaction. This paper presents a method to measure and study link speeds and latencies over mobile operators in latest generation mobile networks.

articleTitle: Advanced Control Strategies for Wind Turbine Blade Pitch Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This article presents the development of a mathematical model for the pitch angle control system of a wind turbine, aimed at optimizing its operation under varying wind speeds. The pitch angle of the blades is a critically important parameter that affects the efficiency of energy generation and the longevity of the equipment. The article thoroughly examines modeling approaches, including the use of linear and nonlinear approximations, as well as adaptive control methods based on feedback. Simulation conducted in the TIA Portal software environment allowed for the identification of optimal control system parameters, ensuring stable turbine operation under different wind loads. The research results demonstrate that the proposed model effectively reduces mechanical stress on the turbine and increases its overall efficiency.

articleTitle: Local Two-Way Amplifying System for Mobile Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The subject of this publication is a presentation of a specific design and efficiency analysis of a two-way amplifying system developed for LTE (4G) mobile networks in the frequency range of 1720 MHz to 1890 MHz. The present study continues the idea for implementation of amplifying systems installed in a local areas around small villages with a weak LTE (4G) signal coverage. The present design applies two amplifying "lines". One is intended to catch the RF signal from the nearest base station, to amplify and transmit it assuring an acceptable signal level coverage over the area surrounded the mobile device. The second one is to amplify and transmit the signal from the mobile device back to the same base station. The main goal of that particular design is to achieve a significant improvement of the baud rate of the data transmission using the mobile LTE (4G) connection.

articleTitle: Optimizing the Area of the Photovoltaic System taking into Account Shading and other Operational Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The article analyzes the main factors affecting the performance of photovoltaic systems. It has been established that shading is one of the largest factors causing a decrease in the amount of energy produced and leads to two significant problems in the operation of photovoltaic modules. The main goal is to optimize the location of photovoltaic modules in a 1 MWp photovoltaic power plant. Three options are compared in terms of annual electricity production, power losses, area occupied by photovoltaic modules, and specific electricity yield. The obtained results show that when installing the photovoltaic modules at an optimal slope, a maximum specific yield of 0.168 MWh/m2/year is obtained with about 24% less area required for installing the photovoltaic modules.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Efficient U-Net Model for Audio Super-Resolution
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Audio super-resolution involves enhancing the quality and resolution of audio signals, particularly by improving their frequency content and overall clarity. In this paper, we explored the design and evaluation of a lightweight deep learning model based on the popular U-Net architecture for the audio super-resolution task. The proposed model consists of two identical parallel subnetworks: one for reconstructing the full spectrogram of the super-resolution signal and another for reconstructing its high-frequency content. The subnetworks are simple stacks of encoder and decoder blocks with skip connections. Our evaluation demonstrated that the proposed model can achieve comparable or better performance in terms of the objective quality of the upscaled audio signal when compared to other models while being 13 times smaller.

articleTitle: Design and Operation Requirements for a Foot and Ankle Prosthesis
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The loss of mobility due to amputation or severe damage to the ankle joint can significantly reduce a person's quality of life. The ankle joint and foot play a key role in maintaining balance, movement, and weight support, making the development of prostheses that restore these functions a critical task in biomedical engineering. This article examines the main design and operational requirements for ankle joint prostheses. It begins by analyzing the anatomical and biomechanical characteristics of the joint, followed by a discussion of conditions that necessitate prosthetic replacement, including traumatic injuries, vascular diseases, and degenerative joint changes. An overview of existing solutions, their limitations, and an analysis of current technological innovations are provided. The article justifies the need for the development of prostheses with optimized weight and mechanical parameters, capable of energy transmission and reproducing natural movements to enhance mobility and user independence.

articleTitle: Energy Management based on Optimal Hybridization and Minimum Hydrogen Consumption: A Case Study of FC-Battery-SC Modular Train
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This paper deals with an energy management strategy for a catenary-free modular train using a combination of fuel cell (FC), battery (BAT) and supercapacitor (SC). The objective is to identify the best sizing with compromising functional constraints to each source appropriately. The strategy first uses an equivalent consumption minimization (ECMS) algorithm to minimize the fuel consumption (hydrogen) while keeping the state of charge of different components in a safe range. Then, particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm is applied to optimize the sizing of the embedded sources. The compared results, simulated in Matlab/ Simulink environment, prove that PSO contributes to effectively reduce the embedded weight by 10% compared to the ECMS sizing results while achieving an appropriate power distribution.

articleTitle: Automatic Personal Annotation from Head Pose in Multi-View Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: We developed an algorithm for automatic personal annotation for multi-view systems. Several problems arise when the annotation process is implemented in such a system. One of these problems is connected to the credibility criterion – the selection of optimal head poses. Another problem is connected to the number of images sufficient for the multi-view system to recognize the individual. An additional challenge is how to organize and store the extracted face images. Our algorithm applies a combination of CNN and SVM for the annotation. With the help of a Kinect sensor, the person is detected and his face is localized. The algorithm annotates the poses on the basis of the three angles of the head – yaw, pitch and roll. They are recorded in the database with the corresponding angles. The neural network was tested first on the CroppedYale B dataset and then on a dataset created by Kinect. After tuning the network’s parameters, almost all images with varying poses were classified correctly. Experiments were also made to find the range of angles, suited for the accurate annotation. With additional tests, the minimal number of images for individuals sufficient to train the network, was explored as well.

articleTitle: An Approach on Modelling of Distributed Overhead Lines for Transient Studies
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: With the increase in the need to maintain uninterrupted power supply, due to sensitive devices in modern industry, more and more attention is paid to the protection of distribution lines in atypical construction conditions. Taking into account that lightning strikes are a frequent and main cause of power interruptions, it is necessary to take into account all the factors that can affect the improvement of the performance of distribution lines. This paper introduces a novel approach by incorporating tower grounding resistance, height, type, surge arrester, and flashover models in conditions of high soil resistance without physical protection. The proposed modelling procedure is validated through simulations on the 35 kV line "Kotor - Lovćen" in Montenegro, characterized by inadequate protection and high soil resistance, using the EMTP software and adhering to IEEE 1410 - 2004 standards.

articleTitle: Leveraging AI for CTF Challenge Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Capture the Flag (CTF) competitions have become integral to developing cybersecurity skills, providing participants with real-world scenarios that challenge their problem-solving abilities. However, the complexity of these challenges often creates barriers for participants, especially those with less experience. This paper explores the potential of leveraging Artificial Intelligence (AI), specifically OpenAI’s Large Language Models (LLMs), to optimize the CTF challenge-solving process. By conducting a comparative study, we analyze how AI can assist participants by offering intelligent hints and personalized suggestions without compromising the integrity of the challenge. Our approach focuses on using pre-trained models to enhance learning outcomes, improve engagement, and streamline problem-solving across different difficulty levels. The results show that AI-driven solutions significantly improve the accessibility and effectiveness of CTF challenges, particularly for novice participants, by creating a more collaborative learning environment. The paper concludes that the integration of AI in CTF competitions can revolutionize cybersecurity education by making it more inclusive and adaptable to a wide range of learners.

articleTitle: A Method for Creating a Criterion-referenced Assessment of Bird Vocalization Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This report presents an analysis of the feasibility of using a method to recognize bird vocalizations. The automated extraction of information from sound recordings collected over extended periods of time is reviewed and a method proposed to improve the scope of biodiversity monitoring. For this purpose, birdsong is automatically segmented into acoustic events and subsequently, for each segment, the areas of increased energy density are determined. After framing the resulting areas, the coordinates and values of the local energy density maxima are determined. Different acoustic events of the same bird song species have varying contour lengths referring to the same syllable type. Therefore, the most compressed information representation of the cycle through a given parametric model is sought. An interpolation model based on GMM with M components is chose. The model parameters are then fed to a classifier to recognize the syllable type of the bird vocalization. The 78 syllables obtained during signal segmentation are classified with ninety-eight percent accuracy, the recognition method and the type of acoustic event are the determining factor.

articleTitle: Mathematical Models for Chlorophyll Prediction in Maize Leaves
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The paper presents mathematical models for chlorophyll prediction in maize leaves using digital images of the plants. Estimation of chlorophyll content is important to determine the phase of plant growth, which depends on what fertilization in cultivated areas will be needed, and to predict the period in which it will be required, which is a major part of precision agriculture. To evaluate the chlorophyll and carotenoids of the plants, digital images in RGB model and their transformation into HSV and Lab are used. A strong correlation between the color components and the three forms of chlorophyll - total, type a and type b - was evaluated and found. Three most informative features for modeling dependencies are selected - for total chlorophyll and chlorophyll type a – V(HSV), R(RGB) and S(HSV) and for chlorophyll type b – V(HSV), R(RGB) and H(HSV). The modeling of these dependencies with eight mathematical models in the Matlab environment is done. The fine tree type model is suitable for predicting total chlorophyll and chlorophyll type b, the coarse tree type model is suitable for predicting chlorophyll type a. To predict carotenoids, it is necessary to select other informative characters from color components or indices. The resulting models for predicting chlorophyll in maize leaves will be supplemented with two more factors influencing plant growth and how they are treated during the individual main growth phases - temperature and humidity - to predict how long the corresponding phase will occur and what it will be necessary to treat the plants in order to obtain a higher yield.

articleTitle: Automated Control of Soil Aeration Machine to Agricultural Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The use of agricultural robots in agriculture is not new. They cancel human labor in bad conditions. Unfortunately, however, the application of this technology in the daily life of farmers is not yet common. This is mainly due to the high cost of the products and the frequent defects that occur during their operation. The use of robots in agriculture is related to the design of specialized equipment for each robot. This equipment is responsible for the accuracy and quality of the technological operations performed by the robot. Soil aeration is one such operation in which the soil is saturated with oxygen and its compaction is avoided. This article offers a variant of automated control to designed soil aeration equipment. The individual modules and elements of this management are considered. An algorithm in the form of a flowchart describing the functioning of the system is given.

articleTitle: Simulator for Technical Diagnostics of an Electrical Substation
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The main attention in the study is devoted to the development in an accessible form of the theoretical foundations of technical diagnostics based on Modeling on the basis of a potential picture. The simulator is implemented on the basis of 3D models with the game engine Unity realistically recreates the most widespread in Bulgaria Electrical substation 110/20kV.

articleTitle: Energy Management Strategy Development for Formula-E Race Cars
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The primary objective of this study is to analyze the energy consumption patterns of Formula E racing cars under various track conditions. Furthermore, the research identifies strategies to extend the driving range of electric vehicles and optimize their energy management, contributing to the development of more efficient electric vehicle technologies. Extensive studies and simulations were performed using MATLAB. A key part of the analysis involves creating a three-dimensional graph of the track, using data on track length and elevation. This graphical representation provided a detailed and realistic basis for the simulations. Real-world data, including the engine and aerodynamic characteristics of Formula E race cars, were used to ensure the accuracy and relevance of the research. A comprehensive physics model has been developed, incorporating various external factors that can affect the car throughout the race, such as track surface conditions, weather effects and drag aerodynamics. These elements have been carefully integrated into the vehicle model using well-established physics equations. The culmination of this research was the development of a complex simulation to investigate the impact of different racing strategies and track conditions on lap times. This study plays a key role in observing and understanding the behavior of Formula E cars on the track, especially in terms of energy consumption.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Mobile NFC Reader and its Application
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This paper will present development and testing of an affordable NFC terminal with wide and versatile capabilities. Due to the growing popularity of that technology, the device presents an easy to work platform for testing and integration of new solutions. Combination of display, keyboard and battery are making it a good fit for mobile IoT gateway.

articleTitle: Examination of the Possibilities of Integration of Control Systems to the Requirements of the "Industry 4.0" Concept of a Single-function Mechatronic Device and of a Multi-function Mechatronic System
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The aim of this work is to investigate the integration of two management systems to the requirements of the "Industry 4.0" concept. In order to achieve this goal, an established methodology for calculating the degree of suitability for the integration of existing industrial process control systems to the requirements of the "Industry 4.0" concept will be approbated by conducting research on the control systems of a single-function mechatronic device and a multi-function mechatronic system. An initial assessment and analysis of the existing situation will be carried out, after which both systems will be upgraded. After the modernization, the suitability of the systems will be estimated again, and the results will be analyzed.

articleTitle: Enhanced Simulation Tool for ZigBee Security
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The significance of ZigBee security is on the rise because of the growing reliance on wireless sensor networks (WSNs) and the need for secure communication. Ensuring security in ZigBee networks involves elements like key management, encryption, and safeguarding data across various stack layers. Developing simulators to replicate and visually represent network security processes is essential for enhancing the security and understanding of these networks. Lately, numerous simulators have been created to assess the efficiency of Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs). However, among the simulators examined, none focused on the communication security of ZigBee devices at the application layer of the ZigBee stack.This paper presents an enhanced simulator to help analyze and improve network security by showing the key generation and exchange process, along with application layer encryption. The simulator employs 128-bit AES encryption in accordance with ZigBee standards and shows a graphical depiction of the application layer key request, generation, and receipt sequence. This allows users to examine diverse security contexts and visualize the results of standard and non-standard operational approaches.

articleTitle: Analysis of Contactless Measurement Accuracy of RFID Transponder Resonant Frequency and Quality Factor
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The article analyses the accuracy of contactless measurement of resonant frequency and quality factor of RFID transponders in a simplified measuring circuit that does not use an impedance meter nor vector network analyser. The described measurement does not use compensation for the influence of the measuring circuit on the results. This creates a systematic measurement error, the value of which is analysed. Such simplified measuring circuit is used for fast testing of the finalized RFID transponders in the factory when contact measurement is no longer possible. The measuring circuit works like a band-stop (notch) filter, and to measure the parameters of RFID transponders, it is sufficient to measure the absolute value of the transfer function, e.g. using a signal generator and a voltage level meter, but a spectrum analyser with a tracking generator can be faster alternative. The results of the analysis show the influence of individual parameters of the measuring circuit, including the parasitic ones, on the accuracy of the resonant frequency and quality factor measurement.

articleTitle: Detection of Livestock using Edge Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This paper presents the development of a real-time system for detecting and monitoring large livestock using cameras connected to a Jetson Nano device and the YOLO v8 model for animal recognition (specifically cattle). The implementation of this system enables precise tracking of livestock movements and conditions, facilitating supervision and management on farms. The system provides real-time notifications and information crucial for efficient resource management. Model evaluation showed an accuracy of 65% after 35 epochs of training. The developed platform demonstrates potential for improving efficiency and safety in agricultural enterprises with possibilities for further enhancement and scaling.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of Hydraulic Energy Recovery System
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The paper explores topics related to the operation and application of hydraulic energy recovery systems. Features of operation and application of different types of power drive machines are considered. The paper presents the results obtained from the testing in laboratory conditions of energy recovery systems operating in open and closed loop. The operation of a stabilizing unit in the system was evaluated and the efficiency coefficient was determined. It is investigated the work of feed pump operating in turbine mode, known as Pumps as Turbines (PAT) in open and closed loop operation. The coefficient of performance was evaluated for the operation of the energy recovery system (ERS) with a stabilizer unit and the ERS composed only of a PAT driven centrifugal pump.

articleTitle: The Stability and Computational Complexity Analysis of Tree-seed Algorithm for Frequency-Constrained 10-bar Truss Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Optimization studies in truss problems produce different results according to different optimization conditions, which leads to significant changes in the results obtained. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the Tree-Seed Algorithm (TSA) in solving the frequency-constrained 10-bar truss optimization problem, a well-known benchmark in structural engineering characterized by its complex, non-linear, and multi-modal design space. The TSA, inspired by natural processes of tree growth and seed dispersion, is evaluated in the truss problem for its stability, computational efficiency, and ability to find optimal solutions. Through rigorous testing involving 51 independent runs, the TSA consistently achieves optimal solutions with a mean objective function value of 554.4549 and a standard deviation of 1.4049. The algorithm demonstrates rapid convergence, typically within 100 iterations. The design parameters of the frequency-constrained 10-bar truss optimization problem were found by TSA within stability. These findings highlight the TSA's effectiveness and reliability, establishing it as a robust tool for tackling complex engineering optimization problems and suggesting its potential for broader applications in structural optimization.

articleTitle: Integration of Heterogeneous IDS with SIEM for DDoS Attack Detection in Computer Networked Multi-Organizational Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The increasing reliance on computer networks for business operations has led to a rise in Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks. These attacks pose significant threats to network security, economic stability, and organizational operations. Organizations connected through the same network are particularly vulnerable. In response to these growing threats, detection systems have been developed to integrate heterogeneous Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) with Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) systems. This integration assists in the detection of DDoS attacks within multi-organizational environments. The system employs the Opensearch dashboard, providing a centralized and efficient interface for the Security Operations Center. System testing was conducted through coordinated DDoS attack simulations by three attackers over a duration of 7-8 minutes. The Snort IDS demonstrated an average detection rate of 95.4%, with an alert correlation mechanism efficiency of 84.6%. Among the IDS systems tested, Zeek IDS consumed the most resources, with an average CPU usage of 24.6% and memory usage of 86.5%. In contrast, the Wazuh Dashboard exhibited lower resource consumption, with an average CPU usage of 0.6% and memory usage of 5.2%.

articleTitle: Using Artificial Neural Networks to Study Dependencies in Real-Time Audio and Video Conferencing
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Real-time research of modern audio and video conferencing in operational conditions is important for revealing bottlenecks in their functioning. On this basis, recommendations can be made to improve performance indicators, such as productivity, reliability, mode of service, etc. In the study, the architecture of the artificial neural network (ANN) of the type with forward feed and backpropagation of errors was chosen. These networks are made up of several layers of neurons: an input layer, several hidden layers, and an output layer. The study used the Levenberg-Marquardt learning algorithm, which combines gradient descent methods and the Gaussian and Newtonian algorithm. The relationship between "active audio streams - active users" with two neural networks was investigated: The first number of neurons in the hidden layer is 5; The second number of neurons in the hidden layer is 6. The activating function that is used for the neurons of the hidden layer is the tangent hyperbolic, and for the output neuron – the linear function. The neural network with six neurons in the hidden layer in the scope of the training sample, the prediction of ANN is very close to the cloud of points of the original data. It can also be seen that in proximity (about 10% of the training sample range) ANN also has some extrapolation ability, reproducing the behavior of the original data.

articleTitle: Designing a CNC Drawing Microprocessor System
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The development of systems for automating machine operations is due to the desire to achieve higher productivity, higher quality and repeatability of the obtained results during processing, as well as independence of production from the qualification of the worker. This paper describes the design of a CNC drafting microprocessor system that is small in size, low in cost, easily controlled by a computer, and can be interrupted or stopped suddenly, with one click of the computer mouse. The main hardware and software components used are: Arduino Uno development board, CNC Shield, stepper motors, simple chemical, Arduino IDE software and Inscape software.

articleTitle: A Novel ZYNQ SoC-based Data Acquisition System for Physical Unclonable Functions
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Physical Unclonable Functions have emerged as essential hardware security primitives, leveraging inherent manufacturing variations to generate unique identifiers for devices. However, comprehensive on-chip characterization has been insufficiently addressed in the literature, particularly regarding data acquisition systems designed to collect CRP data for PUF performance evaluation. In this work, we present a ZYNQ SoC-based data acquisition system specifically tailored for PUFs using the AMD PYNQ framework. The PYNQ platform facilitates the integration of custom IP blocks with the ARM processor using its overlay concept. This approach allows for rapid prototyping without the need to re-synthesize the entire system, thus saving design time. Furthermore, it facilitates the integration of existing projects, making PYNQ a versatile tool for a broad range of applications. Through a detailed use case, we have demonstrated the successful operation of our proposed PUF CRP Data Acquisition System. Our approach extends beyond data acquisition, offering potential future applications in scenarios that require a Hardware-in-the-Loop methodology.

articleTitle: Experimental Study, Simulation and Methods of Transmission Signal in Wireless Communication Systems using Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: One of the most popular modulation methods for wireless communication is orthogonal frequency division multiplexing, or OFDM. Massive data rates with adequate resilience to radio channel failures can be obtained via OFDM. Matlab is used to simulate and study the fundamental processing involved in creating OFDM signals in physical channels. In this instance, one of the Digital Video Broadcasting (DVB) standard's proposed OFDM signals for European Terrestrial Digital Television (DTV) services is utilized as an example.

articleTitle: A Traffic Sign Recognition System using FPGA-Based YOLOv3-Tiny Network
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This paper presents the development of a traffic sign recognition and detection system utilizing the Kria KV260. The system combines hardware and software, with input data collected via camera and processed using the YOLOv3-Tiny network, a model developed by Joseph Redmon. The results are decoded and displayed directly on a screen. The research evaluated and compared models such as RCNN, its enhanced version, YOLOv2, and YOLOv3 to determine the suitable model based on processing speed, accuracy, and model size. After fine-tuning and implementing on the FPGA-SoC (Systemon-Chip), YOLOv3-Tiny was chosen, delivering mean average precision (mAP) of about 94% across 40 data classes, with processing speeds of 20 to 29 FPS on hardware. The study highlights the great potential of deploying a YOLOv3-Tiny-based traffic sign recognition system on FPGA platforms, proposing the way to develop real-time traffic recognition systems.

articleTitle: Optimization of Fractal Antennas for RFID and Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The required antenna design should have a small size, lower weight, and should operate in multiple frequency bands, have high radiation efficiency, and low loss in high frequency while considering the minimum cost. By adopting the fractal geometries to create antenna-radiated elements, the designed antennas have significantly improved antenna features. Firstly, a rectangular microstrip antenna is designed and analyzed for the Radio Frequency Identification system. The reducing dimension of the antenna is achieved using the third iteration of the Koch fractal, which is optimized using Ansoft/HFSS software. Considering the results, the proposed antenna operated a stable radiation pattern at 868 MHz, 2.4 GHz, and 6 GHz. Secondly, the fractal geometry was applied to the antenna radiator. The two-sided, third iteration of the Koch fractal has been used to increase the electrical current path on the radiating element surface. The proposed antenna is printed on an FR-4 substrate with a thickness of 1.6 mm and a relative dielectric constant of 4.4 is fed with a 50-ohm microstrip supply line. The resulting antenna dimensions are approximately 45 mm x 41 mm. The dimensions of the antenna have been determined by using the parametric study to be more efficient. It demonstrates that the antenna offers a multiband performance with many resonance frequencies, including many other communication services, as well as the current 2.4 / 5.8 GHz WLAN applications.

articleTitle: Optimizing Dimensionality Reduction in SDN: A Metaheuristic Approach of UMAP Parameter Tuning
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The reliability and performance of Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) in Software-Defined Networking (SDN) can be significantly improved through effective dimensionality reduction. The Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) is one of the most prominent methods for dimensionality reduction, making it ideal for structured and hierarchical network data. UMAP's performance is critically dependent on fine-tuned parameters such as the number of neighbors, minimum distance between points, and the distance metric, which directly impact the quality of reduced-dimensional space. This paper employs metaheuristic algorithms, including Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Simulated Annealing (SA) to methodically optimize these parameters. The application of these algorithms demonstrates significant improvements in the accuracy and reliability of UMAP, leading to more effective anomaly detection in SDN environments. This research not only enhances the operational efficiency of IDS but also contributes to the body of knowledge by providing a systematic approach to parameter tuning that can be applied to other AI-driven applications.

articleTitle: AI-Generated Text Detection and Prevention of Unethical AI Use in Student Exams
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The widespread use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies based on Large Language Models (LLM) is significantly transforming the educational landscape. While AI is proving its benefits for personalized learning, it also poses serious challenges, especially in terms of assessing students' knowledge during exams and independent work. Tools like ChatGPT can help students generate or refine text, which raises questions about academic honesty.This paper examines the effectiveness of AI text detectors, as well as ways to circumvent them. The focus of the research is on Bulgarian language texts, as there is currently a dearth of such data and revised English and Bulgarian texts in terms of grammar and style only.Effective examination practices should include anti-manipulation measures such as proctoring technologies and authentication. Attendance exam remains the most reliable method of ensuring both academic honesty and important social interactions critical to students' future career development.

articleTitle: Development of a Universal Integrated Monitoring System for Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Monitoring systems are a set of technical tools that continuously monitor and acquire information in a communication network, based on the analysis of statistical data, in order to identify faulty or malfunctioning nodes and processes and to alert the responsible persons. The main objective of this paper is to present the development of a hardware integrated system, mounted in a chassis for embedding in a 19" communications cabinet, which allows the monitoring of the server room in which it is located, by means of built-in sensors, as well as the monitoring of external networks and systems of different types (wireless, optical, etc.) and with different purposes. The applicability and functionality of the developed integrated system for monitoring communication networks is demonstrated through several use cases presented as examples in the paper.

articleTitle: Study of the Attitudes and Interests of Students Studying Design in Bulgaria for Introducing Training in "Design Process Management Methods"
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Modern teaching methods are essential in enhancing students' engagement and interest in their study subjects. In the current educational landscape, the approach to training in each discipline must be multifaceted. It begins with providing students with a strong theoretical foundation, introducing them to the essence and principles that underpin the subject. This includes mastering fundamental concepts and the development of skills necessary to perform effectively in applied environments relevant to their chosen fields. This article examines and analyzes the results of a survey conducted among students studying Design in Bulgaria. The purpose of the research is to determine the attitude and the need for studying "Methods for managing design processes" as a separate study discipline in Bulgarian universities providing education in design disciplines. The obtained results confirm the positive attitude of the students towards studying the proposed discipline, combined with modern teaching methods, which is a prerequisite for increasing the interest of the students and better realization of the labor market.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Power Harvesting by Electrically Small, Resonant, Parasitic, Superdirective Arrays Designed via Characteristic Mode Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The work at hand provides a comprehensive study of Electromagnetic Power Harvesting via Metamaterial type antennas on the context of the Characteristic Mode Theory. Super-directive, parasitic arrays of electrically small but resonant element radiators - particles are studied, designed and evaluated. The presented designs provide more antenna-gain than conventional ones by invoicing and practically matching the theoretical maximum bounds of super-directivity boosting the rectenna system to its absolute limits, as far as the antenna part is concerned. Furthermore, those arrays apart from their own merit they exhibit the characteristic that can be arranged in large host surfaces to scale for even more increased performance. In the current work we will show that the analysis of harvesting particles via Characteristic Mode Theory can provide in-depth understanding of the physics involved and assist on performance improvement strategies during relative design circles.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Feasibility of Creating an Atmospheric Boundary Layer in a Small Wind Tunnel
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Growing focus on renewable energy prompted the Center for Hydro- and Aerodynamics (CHA) to modernize a small wind tunnel with an open test section. This study builds on prior work confirming the feasibility of modifying the test section geometry without disturbing flow velocity. The objective is to explore modeling the atmospheric boundary layer in the new test section. Using theoretical calculations with empirical formulas, followed by CFD simulations, the airflow parameters were optimized. The study graphically presents velocity fields, gradient distributions, and vectors. This modernization enhances potential for experimental research in wind energy, uniquely combining theoretical and CFD approaches to refine geometry and boundary layer development in the test section. Final results confirm the effectiveness of the method for modeling the atmospheric boundary layer in a short test section.

articleTitle: Determination of Greenhouse Gases Emitted by Machine-Tractor Unit by Fuel Consumption
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Any industrial activity carried out by humans is associated with the release of a certain amount of greenhouse gases. These industrial activities during the different stages of the industrial revolution led to an increase in the amount of these greenhouse gases. As a result of the beginning of this revolution until now, the concentration of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere has increased by more than 150%. The increase in the concentration of greenhouse gases as a result of human activity leads to an increase in the average global temperature and to a change in the energy balance of air conditioning systems. Like any human activity, the production of plant products is related to the emission of greenhouse gases. It is mainly expressed in the consumed fuel and in the spills of fuel and lubricants during various technological operations in the cultivation of plants. This article will attempt to determine the amount of greenhouse gases emitted by the tractor when performing various technological operations per unit area. During the experiment, the technological operations of sowing, spraying and fertilizing wheat crops were investigated. The generated greenhouse gases are calculated on the basis of fuel consumed by the tractor during the performance of technological operations. Greenhouse gases have been determined and compared according to a standardized methodology for performing the main technological operations in industrial wheat cultivation. Recommendations for reducing greenhouse gases are given.

articleTitle: Noise Impact Recognition in Fiber-Optic Construct Materials by Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The research examines one of the main problems of ensuring the performance of the transmission medium in the structure of optical routes. The main aspect is consist of the establishment of the noise impact types occurring in the construct materials of optical transmission lines. Gaussian White Noise and Periodic Random Noise in composite Glass and Plastic Optic Fibers were introduced as research objects. Regarding the identification processes of the target noises, an approach based on Machine Learning Methods was created. Different Machine Learning approaches were analyzed in STATISTICA and MATLAB platforms. With the highest confidence degree according to the achieved quantitative and qualitative assessment, Support Vector Machine, k-Nearest Neighbors, Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Interface Systems, Cascade-Forward Neural Networks and Probabilistic Neural Networks. The final synthesis of classification models is tied to the obtained maximum indices of Noise recognition, respectively 85.000 %, 87.100 %, 97.900 %, 99.06166 %, 99.700 % and 100.000 % using the Machine Leaning methods defined.

articleTitle: Recognition of Face Images by DWT, NB, SVM, FFNN and CFNN Methodology
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The paper proposes a conceptual methodology for face recognition, combining phases of extraction of informative features with Discrete Wavelet Transform and identification of images after decomposition with Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence. The Haar, Coiflets, Biorthogonal and Symplets Wavelet Transforms from 2 order were integrated as tools for feature extraction of Approximation and Detail wavelet coefficients. Analytical methods based on Naive Bayes and Support Vector Machine techniques were adapted for manipulations with two personalization classes. An advantage was found when using the Nu-Support Vector Machine approach with different Kernel functions for face recognition procedures. Training was conducted with Gradient techniques in the synthesis of three-layer Feed-Forward Neural Networks and Cascade-Forward Neural Networks in the diagnosis of five face images. Unsuitability of Feed-Forward networks was found when applying Log-sigmoid transfer function in the output layers of the networks. High levels of recognition correctness were obtained with minimization of accepted error criteria when using Cascade-forward and Feed-forward neural networks in Linear and Hyperbolic tangent sigmoid activation of outputs.

articleTitle: Design of Methodology to Calculate the Degree of Suitability for Integration to the Requirements of the "Industry 4.0" Concept
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The aim of this work is to develop a methodology for quantitative calculation of the degree of suitability for integration of industrial process management systems to the requirements of the "Industry 4.0" concept. To achieve this aim, the main steps that make up the methodology will be defined, and the main indicators will be described in them. The main types of scenarios for applying the developed methodology will be developed.

articleTitle: An Analysis of Quantum Technologies Implemented in Encryption Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Quantum technologies have recently undergone a second quantum revolution, following the first that triumphed with the creation of quantum mechanics at the beginning of the twentieth century. Quantum computing promises to solve hard mathematical problems exponentially faster than classical supercomputers, and this poses serious threats to classical cryptography, whose security is based on deterministic hard-to-solve mathematical problems such as the factorial of large integers.

articleTitle: Improved Alkaline Electrode Configuration and CFD Modeling Comparison between Different Electrolysers
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Alkaline electrolysis is the most industrially developed hydrogen production approach. Any improvements of alkaline electrolysers (AEL) are aimed at increasing the efficiency of the system. As a result, the most mature technology ‘classical’ AEL is developed further to Zero-gap AEL by compressing the porous electrodes on both sides of hydroxide anion exchange membrane (AEM) in order to reduce the current losses in the cell. In the present study, an improved AEL electrode configuration is proposed to provide a more compact design and lower electrical losses in the system. This was achieved by increasing the thickness of the electrodes by 10 times and adding hole’s structure. Here, three electrolyser designs: classical AEL, AEM, and an improved AEL were modeled by COMSOL Multiphysics software and compared in polarization curves, hydrogen production and efficiency. All designs feature identical active surface areas of 365 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> for hydrogen production but vary in overall size. Both the classical AEL and AEM designs are with dimensions of 19 cm × 19 cm. In contrast, the improved AEL design has more compact dimensions of 5 cm × 5 cm, achieving the same hydrogen production capacity with a reduction of 53% and 73% in volume size, respectively. It was observed the lowest working temperature at 2.1V operating voltage is 21.3 °C for the new model comparing with AEL and AEM of 27.8 °C and 68 °C respectively. The findings emphasize the importance of design optimisation in enhancing the practicality of electrolyser technologies.

articleTitle: Paper Possibilities of Computer Animation in 3ds Max and Its Application in the Educational Process
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This paper explores the capabilities of the 3ds Max program for creating projects with 3D animation. It provides a detailed description of the stages involved in producing an animated clip, presenting the basic steps and phases of development, including concept, modeling, animation, texturing, and rendering. Practical examples illustrate the potential of animation for creating visually attractive and professional projects.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Electronic System for Monitoring a Vehicle’s Diesel Particulate Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: In this paper, an IoT-based system for DPF filter monitoring is presented. The system consists of a DPF monitoring device and an ODB2 Dongle communicating via Bluetooth interface. The article presents the block diagram and algorithm of the system, as well as a practical implementation of the prototype. An experiment was carried out with a car that had a problem with the particulate filter, and the results obtained showed the performance of the system. The aim of the paper is to develop, implement and test an IoT based DPF monitoring system of a full combustion diesel engine vehicle. The developed DPF Monitoring IoT system is suitable for car diagnostics by service workers and also for monitoring the condition of cars owned by private individuals or companies. It can be expanded, by adding additional functionality, allowing controlling additional car parameters, which is the subject of future research.

articleTitle: Analysis of the PV Energy Potential in the Bulgarian Danube River Region between Ruse and Silistra
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The goal of the study is to assess and compare the photovoltaic energy potential in the central-eastern part of the Bulgarian Danube region between the cities of Ruse and Silistra. To achieve this the solar radiation and the temperature of the environment should be obtained and analyzed. articleTitle: Investigation of the Possibilities of Nitrogen Content Determination in Soil Samples by Means of Hyperspectral Image Analysis in the Near-Infrared Region
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The investigation deals with preliminary assessment of possibilities for determination the amount of nitrogen in soil samples using analysis of hyperspectral images, obtained in near-infrared spectrum region. Nitrogen content assessment is an important issue for determination of the degree of fertilization in cultivated areas, as part of precision agriculture applications. The soil samples are preliminary prepared by adding different amount of CH4N2O in a dry soil and in a soil sample with constant water content. The images of the samples are then captured using N17E hyperspectral camera (Specim LTD, Finland) in the region of 850 ÷ 1700 nm. The hyperspectral images are processed and a set of normalized average spectral characteristics for each soil sample is presented for further analysis. The performance of several mathematical models: PLS, Stochastic Gradient Descent, Decision Tree, Neural Network (Multilayer Perceptron), kNN, AdaBoost, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting and Linear Regression was tested in order to obtain qualitative assessment of nitrogen content in soil samples. The results show that for most of the models the coefficient of determination R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is above 0.6 and for Multilayer Perceptron, Stochastic Gradient Descent and Gradient Boosting it is above 0.9.

articleTitle: Short-term Forecast of Inflows in a Reservoir using Seasonal ARIMA and ANN
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Water resources planning and management, involves as one of the most important aspects, forecasting the inflows in the reservoirs with the highest possible accuracy. The aim of this paper is to forecast the inflow for the next 1, 2, 3, 5, 365 days, based on historical recorded data. Two different methods were applied: one belongs to the classical time series methods, autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA), and the second one is part of artificial intelligence, Artificial Neural Network (ANN), both methods having toolboxes and predefined functions developed in MATLAB and being suitable for forecasting non-stationary time series. Thus, the capabilities of seasonality components integrated in ARIMA method and the ability of ANN to give good results were explored using MATLAB. Inflow values recorded at a large reservoir in Romania were used for calibrating the model. Coefficient of determination, root mean square error (RMSE) and Nash Sutcliffe efficiency have been calculated to estimate the performance of the models. ARIMA, with the seasonal component removed, is well-suited to short-term forecasts. By increasing the forecast time horizon, the accuracy of the predicted values decreases. ARIMA can be used to forecast the inflows for one year prediction horizon but the accuracy is low. For one step ahead forecasting, both methods provide results in good agreement with the original data.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of an Efficient Vedic Multiplier for Complex Multiplier and Complex MAC Unit in DSP Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: In many applications of digital signal processing (DSP) and communication networks, complex multiplication is essential. The efficiency and speed of complex multiplication have a direct and important effect on the overall performance of these systems. To tackle the challenges mentioned above effectively, the present paper puts forth a proposal for a well-thought-out design and execution of a complex multiplier, integrated with its utilization in a Complex Multiply-Accumulate (Complex -MAC) module featuring various bit-sizes (8-16-32-64). These proposals are based on design improved version of Vedic multiplier (IV-VM) and involves the utilization of a hybrid adder that combines an enhanced Han Carlson adder with a carry-select adder (HHC-CSLA). This hybrid adder is employed to carry out addition operations for complex multiplier, and partial products in the Vedic multiplier VM, as well as for computing the sum of products within the complex MAC unit. Using the Xilinx ISE14.7 tool and VHDL language, the suggested designs are generated in several Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) families. All designs have shown significant reductions in latency and space utilization across all devices in terms of performance.

articleTitle: Innovative Conservation of Intangible Cultural Heritage through Motion Capture and 3D Scanning Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: For every nation, conserving its heritage is of greatest importance. While tangible heritage can be easily digitized using 3D scanners, making it accessible permanently, intangible cultural heritage presents a greater challenge in this regard. A prime example is Bulgarian folk dances, which vary uniquely across different regions of Bulgaria, along with the traditional costumes worn during these performances. These traditions are often kept by the older generations, and to ensure their preservation, a combination of 3D scanning and motion capture systems should be employed. This report explores an innovative approach, which allows for the conservation of both the movements of the dances and the detailed models of the costumes.

articleTitle: Internet of Things for Coil-Winding CNC Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The internet of things (IoT) plays an important role in monitoring machines, productions and inventory management in smart factories. It helps to improve labor productivity, automatic system management, and devices maintenance. This paper presents the IoT framework and the results of research, design, and fabrication of the Wi-Fi wireless communication and control IoT system for coil winding CNC machines. A coil winding CNC machine includes three motors: one for releasing winding, one for winding coil and the other for spreading wiring. Each wound- or releasing-winding motor is controlled by an individual inverter, while the spreading winding motor is controlled by a servo drive. The whole electrical drive is monitored and controlled by its Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) including electronic hardware and software. This paper focuses on the design of electronic hardware, communication firmware, and computer and smart phone software for monitoring parameters of a coil winding CNC machine.

articleTitle: Power Quality Impact of DC-DC Converters in Railway Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Energy storage systems offer a solution for energy efficiency and voltage regulation in DC railway systems. For charging the energy storage system within an electrification system, a DC/DC converter is used. The use of SiC MOSFETs in DC/DC converters allows for an increase in switching frequency, which can enhance efficiency. However, this increase can also introduce power quality issues, such as voltage oscillations and overshoot. As the number of electrification systems increases in the railway system, the number of converters also increases. In this study, various scenarios were examined in the railway system, involving the simultaneous and staggered connection of one, three, five, and nine converters. The study evaluated how these configurations affected power quality. Obtained results are presented and discussed, comparing the power quality effects according to the number of DC-DC converters and their switching configurations. According to the results, as the number of converters increases, both overshoot and oscillation values generally increase, suggesting higher voltage spikes and greater oscillations in voltage stability within the railway system. However, varying the switching times can mitigate these effects, potentially reducing overshoot and oscillations.
