This insight will help filter designers assess the impact of converters in railway systems.

articleTitle: Opportunities to Increase the Range of Converted Electric Cars
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This paper proposes a methodology for selecting a suitable mass-produced cars with internal combustion engine to be converted into an electric car with a sufficient range for use not only in the city but also outside. To extend the range, models with low mass and low frontal aerodynamic resistance were chosen. Despite this energy efficient approach, the resulting range of the converted electric cars is about 110 km extra-urban driving at 90 km/h due to the limited mass of the battery from the permissible gross weight of the selected cars. In order to further increase the range, ways were sought to reduce the own mass of the vehicle and the mass of the payload to install a larger battery. Conversions of suitable production cars are considered, where there is an opportunity to reduce the payload mass depending on the application of the converted electric vehicle, as well as conversion of all-wheel drive cars, where only one axle drive is retained, or both axles are driven with two electric motors without using the original heavy and complicated transmission. The range in the various conversions reaches up to 250 km at 90 km/h.

articleTitle: Synchronization of Measuring Devices for Forensic Crash Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The measurement of the dynamic parameters of vehicle motion is usually carried out by measuring the velocity of motion, accelerations and angular velocities in all three axes. For research applications, e.g. the DAS-3 with microwave velocity sensor from Corrsys Datron GmbH (now part of the Kistler Group) and the PicDaq5 from Dr. Steffan Datentechnik GmbH are used for this purpose. If the movement of the vehicle also needs to be documented by video, these three measuring devices need to be synchronized in time, e.g. by light pulses for the video and electrical pulses for the speed and acceleration meters. This paper describes the technical solution of the synchronization device, triggered manually during driving tests or by a ribbon switch in the case of measurements during crash tests.

articleTitle: Improving COVID-19 Forecasts using Hybrid Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The spread of COVID-19 has impacted human life in every aspect. Because of the uncertainty of the virus’s future impact, highly advanced machine learning approaches are needed to enhance the accuracy of COVID-19 forecasts. Therefore, we propose the following hybrid models to address the challenge: CNN-LSTM-Prophet, GRU-LSTM-Prophet, and RNN-LSTM-Prophet. The RNN-LSTM-Prophet model performs the best in predicting daily COVID-19 cases in the United States as it has the lowest MSE, RMSE, and MAE values. Moreover, all of the hybrid models perform better than the individual LSTM and Prophet models. Based on the benchmark results, RNN-LSTM-Prophet performs the best compared to the other models in this study. The hybrid model also performs better than the baseline as the MSE, RMSE, and MAE are lower by 2.48%, 1.24%, and 1.85% respectively. Governments worldwide can use RNN-LSTM-Prophet to better determine COVID-19’s future trajectory and then implement the appropriate policies and protocols. Moreover, the model can be used to deal with new diseases on the rise.

articleTitle: A Survey of the Programming Paradigms used in Programming Languages
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This article aims to explore and classify the programming paradigms (PPs) used in programming languages (PLs). It consists of four parts: a brief introduction, an experimental section analyzing 90 PLs created between 1957 and 2024 based on four criteria. The findings are presented in tables and graphs, including a catalog of PLs, a table mapping PLs to PPs and multi-paradigms, and charts showing the creation of PLs by year, relationships between PPs and PLs, and the use of multi-paradigms in PLs. The study reveals that the years 1980 and 1995 saw the highest number of PLs created. 73% of all considered PLs apply 2 or more styles, with the functional and imperative style being the most applied.

articleTitle: Construction of the Intersection Lines of a Sheet Material Transition and Design of the Unfolding of its Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This report presents a comprehensive review of transitions depending on the mutual location of the foundations of the sections, as well as the construction of transitions of the same cross-section and different sizes, with different sections and placement. In order to optimize the section, two cases of construction of inextensible surfaces based on the specified algorithm were designed and analyzed: expansion of an inextensible surface of the type of the second and higher degree and expansion of a transition between sections of different types and shapes with variable sizes. Based on the obtained results of the research, a three-dimensional model of the device for obtaining a transition from sheet material was designed.

articleTitle: One of the Most Common Causes of Deviations in the Hydraulic Characteristics of Electromagnetic Fuel Injectors
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The presented study provides an in-depth analysis of the root causes leading to deviations in the hydraulic characteristics of electromagnetic injectors commonly employed in modern diesel engines equipped with Common Rail fuel systems. Based on a robust statistical dataset gathered from bench tests conducted in a specialized diesel fuel system repair workshop, the research encompasses a wide range of injectors manufactured by leading global suppliers such as Bosch, Denso, and Delphi. All tests were executed under strictly controlled conditions on a specialized CMX6000X test bench, enabling precise measurement of various parameters characterizing injector performance. Through analysis of the obtained data, several factors contributing to the degradation of injector hydraulic characteristics were identified, including wear of working surfaces, carbon deposits, and failures of the electromagnetic coil. Additionally, the study examines the impact of fuel quality, operating conditions, and injector design on their reliability and durability.

articleTitle: PHP based Database Management Tool
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This paper presents the development and implementation of a PHP-based database management tool designed for educational purposes. The tool aims to provide students and educators with an accessible, user-friendly platform for managing and interacting with databases. Key features include a simplified interface for database operations, enhanced security measures, and performance optimization techniques tailored for educational environments. Through this tool, users can gain practical experience in database management, fostering a deeper understanding of database concepts and operations. The paper also discusses the challenges encountered during development and the solutions implemented to address them, highlighting the tool’s potential as a valuable resource for educational purposes.

articleTitle: Internet of Things − Internet of Coffee Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The Internet of Things concept introduces remote monitoring and management of different devices, collecting data through sensors, connected to controllers and sending commands to actuators. This paper presents a real-life example − a project developed for remote monitoring and management of street coffee machines, located at different places, collecting data for available products inside the machine, errors and warnings generated by the machine and remote controls.

articleTitle: Communication Incidents in Self-Organising Cyber-Physical Energy Systems: Assessing Robustness
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Within Cyber-Physical Energy Systems (CPES), the communication infrastructure affects the performance of the power system, as time delays or data losses impact the system’s functionality. Several communication incidents threaten the robustness of the system. This paper presents an overview of these, classifying them according to several characteristics. In addition, a recommendation on relevant incidents to consider when investigating the communication robustness of CPES is given. Finally, this paper provides an exemplary implementation of an agent-based energy system control use case, considering a communication network and its effects, to showcase the aforementioned contributions. The implementation is applied to evaluate the impacts of the selected incidents, using several metrics. It can be used to evaluate possible or existing control concepts and to assess the overall robustness of a system.

articleTitle: Study of the Application of Wide-area Transistors in Inverter Arc Welders
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This paper discusses the possibilities of using SiC and GaN wide-area transistors in inverter-based arc welders to improve their performance. A simulation study is made with respect to the losses in the transistors and with respect to the output current of inverter arc welders at different power transistors.

Author Keywords: SiC and GaN wide bandgap transistors

articleTitle: Architectural Framework for IoT Driven Data Acquisition and Transmission for Dynamic Assessments of Personal Driving Risk Indicator
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Connected and autonomous vehicles can potentially increase traffic safety by using various information and communication technologies (ICT). Data collected using technologies such as the Internet of Things (IoT) enables better traffic safety based on specific safety indicators. Modeling these indicators implies considering traditional traffic components such as driver-vehicle-road-environment. Eventually, if expressed in a suitable aggregate manner, traffic safety indicators can be presented and displayed to drivers to increase their attention and influence them to make decisions to avoid and mitigate traffic incidents. Existing driving risk assessment models usually consider a limited set of indicators related to individual drivers and their psycho-physical abilities which are important for participation in traffic. Data collected using IoT infrastructure alongside distributed computing and cloud technologies enables an expanded set of traffic safety indicators and a better assessment of driving risk. In this study, the common driver-vehicle-road-environment traffic safety indicators were considered and extended with the same indicators collected from neighboring drivers, weather conditions, surrounding awareness, and driver behavior data. We propose a novel architectural framework to provide dynamic driving risk assessment based on data collected using IoT technologies. The architectural framework provides a foundation for efficient data transmission between multiple sources and their processing, thus enabling the prediction of personal driving risk indicators.

articleTitle: Experimental Comparison of Weight and Cost for MOH and Amorphous Transformer Cores
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: In transformer design, the choice of material for the transformer core is critical because it directly affects efficiency, size, and weight. Amorphous steel and MOH cold-rolled grain-oriented are two common materials used for transformer cores to minimize core losses. Amorphous steel has lower core losses and improved energy efficiency as compared to other traditional materials. The density and weight may differ significantly from MOH cold-rolled grain-oriented steel, which is a high-performance silicon steel with optimized magnetic properties. This study compares the weight of two different core materials (amorphous steel and MOH steel) used in transformer cores based on their magnetic properties, density, and overall performance. The results show that the core losses in the amorphous material are low, which can lead to higher efficiency. However, the weight of the amorphous material is higher compared to MOH steel. The difference in transformer material can have a significant impact on the overall transformer's design, affecting not only the physical dimensions but also the overall cost. The results will help transformer designers to evaluate the importance of material selection in transformer design for balancing efficiency, weight, and cost considerations to meet operational requirements.

articleTitle: Exploring the Effectiveness and Reliability of Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This article presents a comparative analysis of different AI platforms for the same task. Several tests were made - a requirement to generate Python code, generate a text report on the same topic and a request to calculate a value. As a result of an analysis of the returned results, the advantages and disadvantages of each used AI chat have been identified. The main parameters that are the subject of the research described in this paper are the response generation time and the reliability of the returned information. From the research done, it can be concluded that of the investigated chats with artificial intelligence, the fastest in calculating and generating answers is Chat with Ask AI with a time of 6.32 seconds.

articleTitle: Cryptography with Integer Multinumbers
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of a cryptographic algorithm based on integer multinumbers. We discuss the quantum-resistance of this algorithm, and some questions related to its security. In particular, we consider the problem of the generation of public keys for this algorithm, the problem of localization of a possible private key, and the problem of mismatches. Some recommendations for increasing the cryptoresistance of the algorithm are proposed.

articleTitle: Using Asynchronous Programming in C# - Problems, Practical Tips and Scenarios: A Short Review
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Asynchronous programming in C# plays a crucial role in enhancing the performance and responsiveness of modern applications, especially in contexts involving I/O operations, network communications, and database interactions. However, despite these improvements, developers often encounter various challenges when working with asynchronous code, such as improper task management, error handling difficulties, performance issues, and synchronization concerns. This paper addresses some of the most common problems in asynchronous development, including poor task management, error propagation, and potential performance bottlenecks. It also provides practical tips for effectively applying asynchronous patterns in everyday development, drawing on real-world industry scenarios where asynchronous programming offers significant advantages in terms of scalability and application stability. Special attention is given to preventing common mistakes, such as deadlocks and task overproduction (task explosion), along with best practices for improving code readability and maintainability. By thoroughly examining these issues and offering solutions, this paper aims to help developers not only understand the fundamentals of asynchronous programming but also apply advanced techniques for optimizing performance and security. Additionally, the article explores current challenges and future opportunities in the development of asynchronous systems, with a focus on how they can contribute effectively in multithreaded and high-load environments.

articleTitle: Improved Accuracy through Optimised Projectile Flight Control
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This paper discusses the design and implementation of an advanced on-board control system for precise missile trajectory correction. It examines the architecture of the system, detailing the integration of sensors and control mechanisms for real-time adjustments. The 4th order Runge-Kutta method was chosen for its efficiency in solving the missile trajectory equations, ensuring accuracy under complex conditions. A comprehensive mathematical model was developed to account for drag, gravity and wind loads. Flight simulation in MATLAB provided a robust testing environment, with results demonstrating the system's effectiveness in minimizing trajectory deviations and improving targeting accuracy in combat scenarios. These results highlight the potential of the control system to meet defense accuracy requirements.

articleTitle: Maximum Power Point Tracking Based Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithm for Grid-Connected Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) systems are widely acknowledged for their sustainable, plentiful, and eco-friendly energy generation. However, the non-linear behavior of PV cells highlights the vital role of maximum power point tracking (MPPT) methods in optimizing their performance. Traditional MPPT techniques often struggle with partial shading conditions (PSCs). To improve MPPT effectiveness, incorporating artificial intelligence methods like deep reinforcement learning (DRL) can be advantageous. This study introduces a crayfish optimization algorithm (COA) based on DRL, specifically proximal policy optimization (PPO), designed to trail the maximum power point (MPP) of a 1-MW grid-connected PV system that includes an energy storage system (ESS) to alleviate fluctuations in PV output power. The control of the ESS is also optimized using another PPO controller. Additionally, the DRL controllers modify the measured PV voltage and ESS current according to reference values obtained from the COA method and variations in PV output. Simulation results using MATLAB/Simulink demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed MPPT and DRL controllers when compared to the traditional perturb and observe algorithm combined with a proportional-integral controller (P&O-PI). Moreover, the obtained results indicated that the COA-PPO method attained a DC boost converter efficiency of 95.14% and a PCC efficiency of 97.24%. In comparison, the PO-PI method achieved efficiencies of 94.24% and 96.30%, respectively.

articleTitle: Educational Study of Diverse Applications of EMR
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The principle of operation and exploitation parameters of different electromechanical relays - automotive ones and general purpose industrial relays, are studied by means of an especially designed experimental bench. The relays are investigated provisioning diverse conditions - change of the controlled consumers and group operation of the relays. The preliminary measurements reported here show the effectiveness and the capabilities of the system. The presented development can be used in automotive service activities or educational process as an example of the application of modern technologies.

articleTitle: MATLAB Interface for Simulation and Experimental Design of Ultrasonic Levitation
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: One of the many applications of ultrasound transducers is acoustic levitation. This technology has a major advantage: it can manipulate objects contactless, thus being used in various fields, such as microelectronics or biotechnologies. This paper proposes an interactive MATLAB interface to simulate the most important acoustic parameters involved in the ultrasonic levitation phenomenon. The user can adjust the transducer spacing and their number to visualize their effects on the acoustic radiation force, the acoustic pressure field, and the Gor’kov potential. The simulation results were used to design and create an experimental physical system. The tests were done for different distances and numbers of transducers. The best solution was obtained for 36 transducers distributed in concentric circles on the surface of two domes, placed parallel at 20 cm from each other. In addition, a study of ultrasound signals and transducers is made.

articleTitle: Splitter-plates to Reduce Drag and Noise of a Flatback Thick Airfoil for Wind Turbine Blades
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The inboard section of wind turbine blades requires very thick airfoils, whose performance in terms of C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">l</inf> can be improved with a flatback trailing edge in order to reduce the adverse pressure gradient. On the other hand, this solution hugely increases aerodynamic drag and noise, and to address these issues, the use of a splitter-plate has been proposed in the past. However, traditional splitters aligned with the chord-line are unable to avoid a drop in C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">l</inf>, due to the reduction in the degree of cambering of the resulting overall geometry. In this study we use 2D CFD to analyze the behavior of a splitter characterized by a downward slope with respect to the chord-line; it is applied to an airfoil having maximum thickness of 30% and flatback trailing edge thickness of 10%. The results of the investigation, conducted for different lengths and slopes of the splitter and for different Re, show that it is possible to achieve significant reduction in drag (up to 26%), in aerodynamic force fluctuations (up to 90%) and in noise (up to 22 dB), while maintaining the same C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">l</inf> of the clean airfoil thanks to an improvement of the cambering brought by the splitter, if its length and slope are sufficient.

articleTitle: Toward the Future: Sustainable Dialectical Model of Nitrogen and Phosphorus Fertilizer Product
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This study investigates the challenges involved in the development of nitrogen and phosphorus products and their combined characteristics, using a hybrid approach to develop a comprehensive model. The model addresses environmental issues such as greenhouse gas emissions and soil eutrophication, alongside economic trade- offs like production costs and market demand. Significant evidence suggests that improving fertilizer efficiency can reduce environmental impacts while maintaining economic viability. These results contribute to the broader field of precision agriculture, highlighting pathways towards more sustainable agriculture practice. There are used the structured and unstructured interviews with 100 employees at different positions in the research from a big chemical company hierarchy with 1000 employees in order to collect information and define key stakeholders and contradictions between them. Each stakeholder in the fertilizer ecosystem plays a unique role, exerting distinct types of influences on the industry. Creating a diagram for the dialectical model in the area of nitrogen and phosphorus fertilizer production involves outlining the key elements and their interrelationships. Creating a roadmap for sustainable nitrogen and phosphorus fertilizer use involves balancing several key elements: production methods, usage efficiency, environmental impact mitigation, and technological integration. Roadmap aims to address contradictions between them by fostering collaboration across industry, government, and research institutions, all while integrating sustainable practices into the entire lifecycle of fertilizer use.

articleTitle: Spray-deposition of MoS2 Thin Films and Their Application in Biosensors
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: In this work, the influence of the parameters of ultrasonic deposition of water solution of MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> was studied and sensing structures for sweat biomarkers were fabricated using the optimal parameters. The optimal flow rate of the ultrasonically atomized solution was determined to be 0.2 mL/min. Mo and Ni electrodes were deposited by vacuum sputtering and their effect on the response of the produced chemoresistive sensors was investigated. The sensitivity of the structures was measured under the influence of NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, NaCl and MgCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. The most stable response was from sensors with Mo electrodes towards NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>.

articleTitle: Integration of Quantum Encryption Systems into Contemporary Fiber-Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Optical fibers form the backbone of our modern communication systems with ubiquitous use from connecting data centers to long distance links. In many cases, these links are used to transport highly sensitive information. QKD (Quantum Key Distribution) can be an ideal solution to protect data with the highest level of security. QKD systems are designed in such a way as to reduce the resources required for their implementation. They should be easily integrated into already existing optical communication networks without special requirements for optical cables.

articleTitle: Microservice Architecture of Modern eLearning Application
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Learning Management Systems (LMS) have been integral to educational institutions for over 20 years. Technically, an LMS consists of functional components designed to deliver, discuss, explain educational materials, and assess user knowledge through various paradigms such as uploading assignments and online questionnaires. The prolonged and intensive use of such systems emphasizes the importance of their maintainability, allowing the accommodation of new components and the replacement of outdated ones. Over the years, the technological foundation of LMS components has transitioned from early versions of PHP to advanced Java, Python, and JavaScript packages. Data repositories have evolved from local relational databases to shared NoSQL databases. Communication technologies have shifted from NNTP news servers to multiple social applications like WhatsApp and Telegram.In this paper, we present architectural solutions implemented in a modern LMS called WBT-Master. This architecture specifically addresses the maintainability of modern LMS, ensuring they evolve alongside emerging Internet technologies. The practical significance of our work lies in its ability to support very heterogeneous components within a logically unified LMS framework. By discussing the architecture of WBT-Master, we offer a method for incorporating both old and new technological platforms into a single system. Additionally, we use this architecture to interface with cloud services, foster social interactions, and optimize user experience. This contributes to the evolution of E-Learning platforms, offering enhanced and more interactive educational experiences for both learners and educators.

articleTitle: Aspects of Communication in the Consumer-Product Relationship. The Simplicity of Form as the Main Factor
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The visual assessment regarding the type, intended behavior and function of a product is one of three main factors, forming the relationship between the consumer and the product itself. This assessment is performed at many levels - semantic, predictive, sensory, correlation with social status, etc. - all of them staked in the form of the product and its expressiveness. Following the law of economy in nature, simplicity of form is asserted as the main factor. Achieving simplicity requires the application of some basic means, which remain unchanged in the evolution of the design practice. The report clarifies the foundation of visual communication, focusing on the informational expressiveness of the product. A classification of six main compositional elements has been created, which define the simplicity of the form as both a basic requirement and a sought-after outcome - characterized by a small number of form-generating elements, symmetry, simplicity of the geometric model, abstraction through a common contour, abstraction through color, and uniformity of the form-generating elements. The function of contrast has been acknowledged as an essential initial trigger for the communication process between the user and the product.

articleTitle: Scenario-Based Analysis of Technical Efficiency in Local Markets for Low-Voltage Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The resulting shift in load and generation profiles on the low voltage (LV) network poses new risks for distribution system operators (DSOs), including issues like congestion and power quality. To address these risks, two approaches are considered: traditional grid reinforcement or flexibility services. An emerging solution for harnessing flexibility is the development of local markets. This paper is focused on defining scenarios for testing the local market, considering different network conditions (load profiles, available capacity limits in the lines), different market clearing mechanisms, and bids. The LV network under study is a real Slovenian LV network in Luče, currently featuring 9 flexible households and one community battery, as part of the X-FLEX project (Horizon 2020, grant agreement n°863927). The second part involves testing these scenarios and conducting an analysis of the results, ensuring network constraints compliance through power flow simulation (using OpenDSS), and performing a technical analysis of the market design based on these results.

articleTitle: Designing a Laboratory Bench for Measuring Torque
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This material presents the design of a bench for measuring torque on a laboratory experimental set-up. The bench makes accurate, repeatable measurements of couplings, springs and shafts to visualize forces and moments. A measuring instrument M-100 was selected, which is designed to adjust the torque of pneumatic and electric screwdrivers with automatic braking, also serves to test tools such as torque wrenches, to measure the torque of rotating parts, as well as to systematize of extensive production processes. For forces in the range 0.3-11.3Nm and purity up to 600Hz. The experimental setup created measures a shaft up to 0.75 m and with a fastening diameter of up to 16mm. Tests performed show agreement between measured and calculated values under static load. In dynamic measurement, a decrease in torque was recorded when the rotation speed increased. The proposed torque stand provides an opportunity to visualize the theoretical material.

articleTitle: Statistical Processing of Data from the Operation of a Wind Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Paper concerns the use of renewable energy source – wind energy. The aim is formulated as data processing of energy generated by a specific wind power plant installed in the Central Balkan Mountain region in the Republic of Bulgaria. Calculations have been performed based on data acquisition values. Conclusions have been drawn based on the results obtained, that the produced and sold active energy significantly differs from the installed capacity. The role of preventive maintenance in order to achieve the planned electricity output is emphasized.

articleTitle: Charging Infrastructure and E-mobility Integration: Economic and Energy Benefits for Sustainable Grid Management
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: In order to fully exploit the potential of renewable energy sources (RES), integrated into existing electricity grids, significant technological and infrastructural improvements or grid renovations are required, as well as the development of intelligent systems for real-time management of energy flows at the connection points. EVs charging infrastructure, due to its technological characteristics, has a large but not fully exploited potential for regulatory and financial functions in this direction. This paper discusses the economic benefits of the impact of EVs and charging infrastructure on grids with an increasing share of RES in the energy mix of countries in energy transition. Another aim of the paper is to prove some concepts and models to tackle the challenge of integrating charging stations into existing electricity grids. There are approaches to solve the load-balancing problem through battery storage. Economically, battery storage is expensive to install and maintain, but has the advantage of being demand-responsive. V2G technology is an optimal solution, but with a charging station infrastructure under construction, which is currently happening in Bulgaria.

articleTitle: Monitoring of Induction 3-Phase Electric Motor under Different Conditions of Operation with the Help of Infrared Thermal Camera
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Especially today electrical motors are necessary part of our life and are presence nearly in every residential or industrial application. Monitoring of these motors is essential, mainly in critical applications, in order to ensure that operates under the normal operations conditions. The measurement of the temperature of the motors is the key point in this direction because overheating is the most common cause of motor failure. In this article, an infrared thermal camera has been used for the depiction of the thermal behavior of an induction 3-phase electric motor under different conditions of operation. The measurements have been implemented in the most sensitive part of the electrical motor, the windings because in this part occurs the highest temperatures. Based on the results, it is clear that an infrared thermal camera is a worthwhile tool to examine an electric motor.

articleTitle: Analysis of Selecting an Active Mechanical Energy Storage System for Household Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Energy storage, regardless of its form, always involves some degree of loss. Therefore, it is most beneficial to generate only as much energy as is required to meet demand. Such a situation in energy systems is very rare and typically lasts for a very short period of time. These are usually transitional states. As a result, the use of energy storage systems is necessary. The issue of grid destabilization becomes particularly important with the use of renewable energy sourced from micro photovoltaic installations and small-scale wind turbines. The high variability in the amount of energy produced often necessitates the automatic disconnection of the installation from the power grid, which results in a reduction in the amount of energy generated. Therefore, energy storage systems are essential to improve the cooperation of micro-installations with the grid. Currently, there are many energy storage solutions available on the market for this purpose, but chemical storage systems such as lithium-ion batteries are most commonly used. These are relatively expensive solutions considering their operational lifespan. Mechanical storage systems offer greater durability; however, their performance characteristics are closely tied to their geometric dimensions. In this context, this article analyzes the operational requirements of an energy system within a household environment and evaluates the size of the necessary mechanical energy storage system.

articleTitle: Exploring the Magic of Reed-Solomon Codes: A Captivating Journey into Encoding Process
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Reed-Solomon codes serve as a cornerstone in the field of error correction coding, offering a robust solution for ensuring data integrity in various communication systems. Despite their significance, students often encounter challenges in comprehending the intricate theory underlying Reed-Solomon codes. This paper delves into the complexities that students face when learning about Reed-Solomon codes, such as the mathematical intricacies involved in the encoding process. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an innovative approach to teaching Reed-Solomon codes that focuses on enhancing student engagement and understanding. By incorporating visually stimulating graphics, real-world examples, and interactive simulations, students can visualize the encoding operations, thereby facilitating a more intuitive grasp of the concepts. Furthermore, practical applications and case studies will be utilized to demonstrate the practical relevance of Reed-Solomon codes in modern communication technologies. Through this comprehensive and immersive learning experience, students will not only gain a deeper understanding of Reed-Solomon codes but also develop the skills necessary to apply this knowledge effectively in real-world scenarios. This paper aims to empower students to navigate the complexities of Reed-Solomon coding with confidence and proficiency.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis and Optimization of Shaded 12.6 kW Peak Photovoltaic System using PVsyst
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The world climate changes and brings severe storms, floodings and other anomalies. The green deal pushes the adoption of green technologies. One of the promising solutions are the photovoltaic (PV) systems, but they still have many drawbacks, which could be overcome by local to the final consumer installations, but most of the human population live in urban areas, where the PV working conditions are far from optimal. The mentioned problems require case-oriented PV system design approaches for optimal operation and lower usage costs. In this regard, a specialized software could be of a big help for at least partial automation of each particular design process. This work analyzes shaded 12.6 kW peak photovoltaic system, located at University of Ruse, installed in urban environment, by using the specialized PVsyst software. The simulation results are compared to the real ones. The conclusions are that the projected results, presented by the PVsyst software, are sufficiently detailed, correct, reliable and useful for the preliminary optimal design process of a PV system for urban environment.

articleTitle: Utilization of Basic Methods for Filling Missing Data from Wastewater Treatment Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The article examines the possibilities for big data analysis, focusing on dealing with missing data. By exploring the techniques and methodologies used for imputation, interpretation, and modeling of missing data in the context of big data analytics, we emphasize the relationship between data completeness and the quality of solutions. The ability to effectively handle missing data not only enhances the reliability and validity of analytical insights but also enables informed strategic decision-making. An experiment was conducted on filling missing data in a dataset based on three different mathematical models. The best result is reported with the autoregressive recursive interpolation model. For this purpose, data from a wastewater treatment plant, which have not been the subject of research so far, were used.

articleTitle: Visual Dynamism of Images and Compositions in a Two-Dimensional Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The report presents opportunities for creating and enhancing the visual dynamism of images and compositions in a two-dimensional environment. Visual perception of the content within compositions requires increasingly less time, according to contemporary analysts. Today's communication culture prefers motion pictures and video content. This leads to the necessity of updating graphic design tools and creating images and compositions in a two-dimensional space. The qualitative characteristics of composition in design have been analyzed - those that contribute to its imagery and expressiveness. The results have been utilized to create a systematization of techniques for constructing dynamic forms and compositions through simple operations. This systematization is rooted in the use of basic geometric shapes. It is not unique but represents a working set of tools illustrated by the corresponding example images.

articleTitle: Identification of PMU Measurements-Based Low-Frequency Oscillation Modes in the IEEE 39 Bus System via DMD
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The implementation of phasor measurement units (PMUs) in power grids has revolutionized the monitoring and management of power systems, allowing for precise voltage and current phasor measurements at high sampling rates. However, the increasing complexity and interconnectivity of power systems have led to the emergence of low-frequency oscillations, posing a significant threat to system stability. This article explores the use of the Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD) algorithm to accurately identify these oscillation modes from PMU measurements. Early detection of these oscillations is crucial for preventing potential blackouts and minimizing economic and societal impacts. The DMD technique is applied to an IEEE 10-Machine, 39-Bus system subjected to a fault, with real power flow measurements taken over specific lines. The methodology includes data collection, processing, and mode identification using the DMD algorithm. The algorithm effectively identifies dominant oscillation modes, their frequencies, and damping ratios, showcasing its potential for system analysis and control. This study demonstrates the applicability of the DMD algorithm to other power systems and its potential for real-time application and analysis of measurement noise impact.

articleTitle: Assessment of Formaldehyde and TVOC Pollution from Laminate Burning in Buildings
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Building fires cause a lot of damage. In the presented work, an experimental study was made of 7 saw laminates, which were subjected to 5 different burning temperatures - 150, 250, 400, 550 and 700<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>C. Each of the samples was kept in the oven for 5 minutes after reaching the set temperature and the formaldehyde concentration was measured three times. An analysis of the obtained results was made and recommendations were given to the interested parties. The aim is to investigate what amount of harmful substances are released when fires occur in buildings

articleTitle: Modelling a Test-rig for Utilization of Wave Energy with Hydrokinetic Turbines
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The present paper presents the modeling of an experimental setup using wave energy - both marine and oceanic. A mathematical calculation of the water wedge of this system is made and a method of making realizing the hydrokinetic turbines, which are planned to be studied in future articles, is also presented.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation the Effect of Number of Blades of Hydrokinetic Turbine Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The kinetic energy of flowing water is harnessed using devices known as hydrokinetic turbines (HT). The main parameters of this type of turbine are given in the presented Work. Experimental research was done on seven turbines with different number of blades and geometry at three different current velocities -0.1, 0.2 and 0.3 m/s. Based on the results obtained from the experimental studies, the main parameters were calculated and analyzed in order to determine the influence of the number of blades on the efficiency of a similar type of turbine.

articleTitle: Detection of Anomalies in Compressed Air Systems using Time of Occurrence and KPI Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Compressed air systems are widely used in industry, but they represent an expensive form of energy and are prone to inefficiencies. This paper presents two novel, non-invasive data-driven approaches for anomaly detection in compressed air systems, focusing on analysing pressure drop curves extracted from pressure signals. The methods, based on time anomalies and a Key Performance Indicator (KPI), identify pressure drops occurring at irregular times or exhibiting unusual curve patterns. This study, utilizing eight datasets from various industrial sources, demonstrates how anomalies can be indicated by the presented methods. Our findings show that the time-based method successfully identifies unusual timing patterns, while the KPI-based method faced limitations, as some detected anomalies may be the result of manual interventions or operational changes. These methods provide a cost-effective solution for anomaly detection without additional interruptions or specialized equipment, as data can be collected during normal operation and the analysis can be conducted in real time, improving energy efficiency and sustainability in compressed air systems.

articleTitle: Fallback Communication System for Drones in Medical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The project KIMoNo is a research project that focuses on the implementation of transporting medical products and samples using a vertical take-off and landing unmanned aerial vehicle (VTOL UAV) for patients in rural and remote areas. The cellular network coverage issue in remote areas limits UAVs to operate only in urban areas. To ensure effective communication between UAVs and a ground team even in remote areas, a fallback communication system is implemented in this paper. A web-based monitoring system is also designed that will allow authorized third parties (e.g. doctors, lab employees) to monitor the status of the UAVs during missions.

articleTitle: Analysis of Energy Potential of Micro Wind Turbines at Three Locations in the Central-Eastern Part of the Bulgarian Danube River Region
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The share of renewable energy sources in the energy mix worldwide is gradually increasing. And even though they all have a highly variable nature, they can be forecasted statistically. The wind energy potential was investigated in this article in the Bulgarian Danube region, located between Ruse and Silistra. Two years of meteorological data, including the wind speed at 10 m height and the ambient temperature was used to estimate the average wind energy for each month of the year at three geographic locations – Ruse, Staro Selo (near Tutrakan), and Calarasi, Romania (near Silistra). The results showed that Staro Selo has the highest energy potential, reaching up to 0.75 kWh/day/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> in February, followed by Calarasi with 0.38 kWh/day/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The city of Ruse showed the lowest wind potential with the highest average monthly value reaching only 0.0027 kWh/day/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The obtained results showed that the regions around Tutrakan and Silistra are appropriate for the application of micro wind turbines.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Root Cause for Insulator Failure through Investigating the Insulator Performance under Environmental Stresses
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Previous investigations result with issues regarding insulators premature aging and degradation process. Recent case of an outage in power plant showed unusual pattern of insulator failure. Insulators operating under various adverse conditions including presence of water, fog, dew and other contaminants are affected by these factors in a way that field enhancement that leads to flashover activity is generated. To identify the root cause of the insulator failure, the service conditions of a polymer rod type 110 kV insulator were simulated using COMSOL Multiphysics (Mph). Simulations relate to presence of water droplets, uniform and non-uniform pollution layer on the insulator surface, and formation of dry band areas. In order to simulate various types of pollutants present on the insulator surface, the pollution layer is modeled as a conductive layer for different values of conductivity. The provided results in the paper, pointing out critical weakened spots due to presence of various contaminants, should be used as a detection tool to determine whether this type of stresses could have contributed to the unusual mechanism of insulator failure. Deeper understanding and knowledge of the failure mechanism may be useful in order to prevent early failures of insulating systems in general.

articleTitle: Application of AI to Develop a Digital Twin of Energy Communities: Conceptual Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Until recently, the real-time virtual representation of energy objects has been limited by the partial integration of AI and the lack of harmonized protocols and standards. Digital twins are a solution for energy objects with high-energy intensity and energy consumption, objects with high economic, social and energy impact. A very important feature and major advantage of digital twins is their scalability. This advantage makes it easier to build and deploy digital twins of micro- and nano-smart grids in energy communities. This enables efficient management of large flows of renewable energy and establishes the place and role of Energy Societies as energy arbiters in a fully liberalised energy market. This article outlines the main steps in building digital twins in an energy community and systematises the latest legislation regulating this process.

articleTitle: Web Application based on Serverless Architecture to Support Group Decision-Making by Scoring Models
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Group decision support systems can facilitate participants in the complex decision-making process. For this purpose, it is necessary to determine two conditions in advance, namely the method of aggregating the preferences of the interested parties and the software architecture on the basis of which the application will be implemented. In this context, the present paper proposes an approach to support group decision-making based on scoring models. Considering the specifics of these patterns, the proposed web application software architecture is implemented serverless, client-only. It is based on a Model-View-Controller design, to manage decision-making processes entirely within the browser of the user. This architecture supports dynamic, interactive decision-making while minimizing the need for backend infrastructure. The applicability of the proposed approach is numerically tested in personnel evaluation and selection. The simulated decision-making scenarios concern the evaluation of ten candidates by a panel of three experts on seven criteria, five of which are objective and the rest subjective.

articleTitle: Research of the Reliability of Interlocking Stations in Railway Transport
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The reliability of the interlocking stations in railway transport is very important, as it is related to ensuring failure-free operation. These devices perform multiple functions and there is a constant interaction between them and the signalling systems in the process of work. A possible failure even in one device should not disrupt the proper functioning of the system as a whole. This determines the particular importance of the problem of the interlocking stations reliability. In this paper, an approach for the analysis of failures of the interlocking stations in railway transport is presented. Firstly, statistical analysis of failures was carried out. Then an analysis of the reliability was made and the reliability indicators are determined.

articleTitle: Seasonal Coefficient of Performance of Air-to-Air Heat Pumps Influence on the Energy Performance of Multifamily Residential Buildings in Bulgaria
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: One of the most used ways to achieve nearly-zero energy buildings (nZEB) in relation to Bulgarian legislation is by the use of air-to-air heat pumps for heating. Specifically for residential and light commercial applications, split type air-to-air heat pumps are widely used. In this regard, this study aims to find how the difference between Seasonal Coefficient of Performance (SCOP) declared by the manufacturer and SCOP recalculated based on the local climate data affects the energy consumption of the buildings. The calculations were made for multifamily residential buildings with different geometry and area for all 9 climatic zones in Bulgaria. The results show that mono-split air-to-air heat pumps used for heating, can actually provide only from 17.9 to 44.9% of the required energy, which is considered as renewable, as the recalculated SCOP can be up to 25.6% lower than declared. An incensement in SCOP with 12.5% can lead to an incensement in the share of renewable energy with about 2%.

articleTitle: AI Driven Innovation for Boosting Performance and efficiency in Mobile and Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The escalating complexity and data volume in today’s digital networks demands innovative strategies to enhance performance and efficiency. This survey explores the possibilities of optimization techniques powered by AI to address this critical need. By utilizing artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms, including machine learning and deep learning, the study explores how AI can transform network optimization and management, to achieve superior performance and reliability. The investigation focuses on how AI algorithms can process extensive network data, recognize patterns, and make informed decisions to enhance network configurations and resource allocation methods. The review highlights key findings and insights, emphasizing the revolutionary impact of AI-based optimization for improving network performance and efficiency. It focuses on the advantages of AI-based methods in power control and EE efficiency, resource allocations, user connection, intelligent beam management, and channel estimation, by automating optimization processes, minimizing operational costs, and flexibly adjusting to evolving network conditions and user requirements. Furthermore, the review addresses the concerns and aspects associated with implementing AI-driven optimization techniques. In conclusion, the review underscores the crucial role of AI-driven optimization in tackling the growing complexities of network optimizations. It advocates for continuous exploration and innovation initiatives to fully harness the potential of AI-driven optimization, unlocking enhanced performance and operational efficiency in network systems.

articleTitle: Technical Review on Dust Removal Materials and Technologies for Solar Panels Maintainance
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The prefeasibility studies, related to the development of PV (photovoltaic) powerplants, are usually based on the estimated energy production form these facilities. The produced energy depends both on the amount of solar radiation and on the specifics of the local geographic and atmospheric conditions. Meanwhile, large number of industrial enterprises are serious generators of dust particles, as a result of their activities. With the appropriate wind speed and direction, these particles can be carried and accumulated over various parts of the surrounding topology or over the solar panel systems. This accumulation, combined with high relative humidity or rain and snowfall, results in the formation of thin non-transparent layer, which hardens over time and can significantly reduce the energy production of the power park by at least 10%. This necessitates the use of different technologies and materials for cleaning the panels, which should be effective, not damaging the absorbent surface of the panels, as well as ensuring sustainable clean surface, when using them. In the presented work, the existing and innovative panel cleaning materials and technologies, which operate in highly dusty environments, are selected and critically analyzed. Conclusions in terms of their effectiveness and applicability is carried out, based on predefined and described methodology.

articleTitle: An Overview of Monitoring Systems, Methods, and Technologies for Hybrid Renewable Energy Sources
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: With the global demand for sustainable energy solutions rising, hybrid renewable energy sources (HRES) are gaining popularity due to their reliability and cost-effectiveness. Effective monitoring systems using sensors and data analytics are essential for optimizing the performance of these systems, ensuring energy efficiency, and predicting maintenance needs. Various monitoring technologies, including SCADA, IoT-based platforms, and cloud storage systems, have been analyzed for their suitability in real-time data acquisition and control of energy systems. The paper examines the critical role of sensor, information, and communication technologies in managing hybrid renewable energy systems (RES), and also reviews several case studies and implementations of energy monitoring systems, emphasizing the importance of integrating these technologies to improve the operational efficiency of HRES.

articleTitle: Lung Cancer Detection in Radiological Imaging using Deep Learning: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Lung cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related deaths globally, requiring creative methods to improve detection efficiency. Data quantity and quality, algorithm complexity, integration into healthcare workflows, and ethical and legal issues are some of the challenges facing artificial intelligence (AI). The study aims to provide a comprehensive overview of state-of-the-art deep learning techniques, in particular Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), for the diagnosis of lung cancer using medical imaging modalities such as Computed Tomography CT scans and X-rays. Some of the primary objectives are to assess algorithm performance, identify gaps and trends, enhance clinical applications, and propose new research directions. To focus future research efforts on more useful solutions, the paper also discusses the need for a larger range of datasets and improved model interpretability. It also considers how deep learning technology could be incorporated into routine screenings to improve patient outcomes and early detection rates. More stable datasets, improved algorithm performance, and the development of morally sound AI deployment frameworks for use in healthcare environments are some of the next directions to pursue. With increasingly powerful diagnostic instruments, notably Computer-Aided Diagnosis (CAD) systems, scholars and practitioners should acquire valuable insights from this investigation, which will ultimately improve patient treatment.

articleTitle: Cloud-Based Smart Home Monitoring using ThingSpeak and ESP32
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This paper presents an approach to implementing a cloud-based smart home monitoring system using the ESP32 microcontroller and ThingSpeak as the cloud platform. The proposed system provides an efficient solution for real-time monitoring of various environmental parameters, which are collected through sensors connected to the ESP32 and transmitted wirelessly to the ThingSpeak cloud. By leveraging the Internet of Things (IoT), this system enables users to remotely monitor their home environment from anywhere using a web interface. The article discusses the hardware setup, software implementation, and data visualization techniques, offering a practical guide for those interested in smart home technology and IoT integration.

articleTitle: Design and Comparison of Control Methods for Grid-Connected Solar Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This paper presents the results of comparing control methods for a single-phase grid-connected converter with a two-stage structure (DC-DC and DC-AC) in solar power application. The DC-DC stage plays an important role in optimizing capacity based on the maximum power point tracking (MPPT) on the solar panel. The Perturb & Observe (P&O) method is used for the DC-DC converter to find the maximum power point. DC-DC converter transmits power from a low DC voltage side to higher DC voltage side compling with the requirements for the DC-AC converter working properly. The DC-AC stage with the L filter has the role of receiving power from the DC-DC converter and transmitting power to the grid. There are some methods to control a DC-AC grid-connected converter. In this paper the three typical control methods, namely voltage-oriented control (VOC), proportional resonant controller-based control (PRC), and flexible power control (FPC) are presented and compared to point out the merits and disadvantages of each technique. As a result, the insight and application range of each control technique are provided. Converters are implemented and tested in Matlab-Simulink platform so that results are reliable.

articleTitle: Using Reinforcement Learning for Optimizing Energy Consumed by Base Stations
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: As mobile communication networks expand rapidly, optimizing their performance becomes crucial. This paper investigates the use of reinforcement learning (RL) to dynamically manage base stations (BS) and sector coverage in response to real-time network demands. Our RL models learn to power down and reactivate BS based on user demand and adjust sector coverage to maintain service quality. Validated using real-world data, our approach demonstrates improvements in adaptability and performance. The results highlight the effectiveness of RL in balancing operational efficiency with service quality and its resilience to evolving network conditions.

articleTitle: Study of a Reverse Electrodialysis Plant Operation on Industrial Liquid Waste
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Reverse electrodialysis (RED) technology is one of the development directions in electrochemistry in the field of membrane processes, namely, electrodialysis, which is widely used in industry and has many areas of industrial use, including a well-developed direction of cleaning wastewater with various compositions. RED has expanded this range of applications thanks to the technology of wastewater treatment with simultaneous generation of electricity. Highly concentrated solutions suitable as working solutions for RED can be obtained as liquid waste in a number of industrial activities. In general, this is a promising prospect for RED as a reliable energy source, as soon as the technological problems are solved. The article presents an analysis of literature data on the use of industrial wastewater as feed solutions for reverse electrodialysis, as well as own experimental studies and results on the processing of liquid waste from a chemically desalting ion exchange water treatment plant of a thermal power plant with the generation of electricity by the reverse electrodialysis method.

articleTitle: Models and Methodologies for Collecting, Processing, and Storing Heterogeneous IoT Data in the Field of Renewable Energy – а Review
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This paper examines the models and methodologies for collecting, processing, and storing heterogeneous Internet of Things (IoT) data in the field of renewable energy. IoT technology plays a crucial role in the energy management of renewable sources such as solar, wind, and hydroelectric systems by enabling real-time monitoring and control. The study explores various data models, including those for data acquisition, prediction, and energy flow management, all of which are essential for optimizing energy production, distribution, and consumption. By integrating IoT with advanced data analytics and machine learning, energy systems can achieve greater efficiency, reduce operational costs, and support the development of smart grids. Key challenges discussed include the need for standardization of communication protocols and ensuring data security, as IoT systems handle sensitive energy information. This research highlights IoT's potential to drive innovation in renewable energy management and contribute to global sustainability goals by enhancing resource efficiency and reducing carbon emissions.

articleTitle: Probabilistic and Deterministic Full Duplex Routing Protocol in Cognitive Radio Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The paper proposes probabilistic and deterministic full duplex routing protocols for cognitive radio networks (CRNs) that address challenges posed by recent advances in full-duplex (FD) communications. Traditional routing schemes face limitations in multi-hop CRNs due to the constrained set of available channels and the half-duplex nature of connections. The proposed protocol leverages full-duplex technology and cognitive radio capabilities to enable efficient spectrum utilization. By considering all channels, including periodically sensed and probabilistically available ones, and assuming full-duplex operation, the protocols aim to optimize throughput. Simulation results demonstrate significant improvements over existing methods, with the proposed protocol achieving higher throughput (approximately 50% more than existing methods). These findings validate the effectiveness of the proposed routing protocols in enhancing the performance of CRNs.

articleTitle: Design of an FPGA-Based System-on-Module for Safety-Critical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Ensuring reliability and safety in safety-critical applications requires measures to mitigate both systematic and random failures. Controlling random failures depends on systematic efforts in developing fault-tolerant or self-testing capable system architectures. Modern safety-related systems are tailored to comply with functional safety standards including IEC 61508 for generic applications, along with industry-specific variants such as EN 5012X series for railway and ISO 26262 for the automotive sector. In this paper, we introduce a Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA)-based System-on-Module (SoM) hardware architecture with built-in self-testing (BIST) and fault-tolerance capabilities to handle random mission phase failures in safety-critical missions. The proposed SoM can differentiate between different system faults and take tailored corrective actions. The SoM is designed with the aim of rapid re-use in various projects and missions aimed at railway, automotive, and related fields that have functional safety requirements. We provide explanations of hardware architecture and underlying rationale, with a particular focus on safety-related functions and subsystems. We also provide a Failure Modes, Effects, and Diagnostics Analysis (FMEDA) study of the proposed system. Our study offers insights into the integration of functional safety requirements into complex electronic systems, highlighting the advantages posed by the modularization of safety-related systems including but not limited to lower development costs, better supply chain resiliency, and better time to market. Finally, it fills the gap for a BIST-capable FPGA hardware platform for conducting safety-related software research and development.

articleTitle: Novel Pulse Generator for Advanced TMS Applications: A Multilevel Converter Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This paper presents the development and evaluation of a novel pulse generator, specifically designed for high-current pulse applications, such as in Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS). The system integrates a multilevel converter with six half-bridge Submodules (SMs), an external H-bridge Polarity Inverter (PI), and a dedicated charge circuit, thereby enabling the generation of 13 distinct voltage levels, including negative pulses.The optimal pulse profiles were determined through simulation studies and subsequently validated through hardware tests. The system achieved a maximum pulse current of 588 A, surpassing the targeted 560A without any damage. The effective parasitic inductances were calculated to be within the range of 0.73 nH to 2.45 nH for the SMs. In contrast, the H-bridge PI exhibited higher parasitic inductances, with a range of 320 nH to 360 nH. The elevated voltage overshoots observed in this system can be attributed to the higher inductance present in the PI.The pulse generator’s design allows for the generation of customisable pulse shapes and durations, enhancing its versatility for applications such as TMS. Future improvements will focus on optimising the layout, increasing voltage and current ratings, and further minimising parasitic effects.

articleTitle: Synthesizing Multi-Modal Imaging for Enhanced Brain Mapping in Neurology: A State-of-the-art Review
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Neuroimaging has significantly advanced our understanding of brain structure and function in both healthy and diseased states. However, due to the brain's complexity, a comprehensive approach involving multiple imaging techniques is necessary. This review provides an overview of the integration of various imaging modalities in neurology, particularly focusing on their applications in mapping the brain. It discusses how combining structural, functional, and molecular imaging methods such as Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), Positron Emission Tomography (PET), and Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) allows for a more thorough examination of brain anatomy, connectivity, and understanding, thereby improving diagnosis and treatment effectiveness in neurological disorders. The review also explores recent progress in image acquisition, data fusion, and computational techniques that facilitate the integration of multimodal imaging data. Additionally, it examines emerging trends like machine learning and artificial intelligence, which offer potential for automating image analysis and identifying new disease biomarkers. Finally, by addressing challenges and future directions in the field, including the need for standardized protocols, initiatives for data sharing, and ethical considerations.

articleTitle: Forecasting Final Energy Consumption in the European Union with Exponential Smoothing
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Optimising final energy consumption is the key to reducing the adverse impact of human activity on the environment and limiting climate change. The capability of forecasting the energy consumption of the economy of each of the Member States of the European Union is a prerequisite for the development of policies for adequate behaviour in the energy market. This paper aims to evaluate exponential smoothing forecasts of final energy consumption for 27 EU countries using annual time series data from Eurostat’s Simplified Energy Balances for the period 1990–2022. We consider exponential smoothing in its evolution from methods to state-space models, outlining its advantages with respect to forecasting a large number of indicators in a relatively accurate, automated and easy-to-interpret way. We estimate non-seasonal exponential models for 244 time series with maximum likelihood and select the best models based on the corrected Akaike Information Criterion. Further, we diagnose the model residuals with the Box-Ljung test. We compare the forecasting performance of the exponential smoothing models to mean, naïve, drift and auto arima models. We evaluate forecast accuracy using cross-validation on the basis of root mean square error.

articleTitle: Integration of 3D Scanning Data and Motion Capture System for Meta Human Animations
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: As digital ecosystems evolve, advanced technologies such as 3D scanning and motion capture are increasingly used, enabling new forms of creative expression. This report explores the significant capabilities that the Artec Leo 3D scanner and Optitrack motion capture system provide for creating Meta-Humans. The potential of these tools within smart digital ecosystems is analyzed, particularly in terms of improving realism, efficiency and interoperability across different digital arts and animation platforms. An overview of the technical capabilities of the Artec Leo scanner and the Optitrack system is presented, emphasizing how these technologies are suited to the creation and animation of Meta Humans. The methodology describes the process of scanning human models using the Artec Leo scanner and then animating them with motion capture data from Optitrack, illustrating how workflows are facilitated. The results show how this integration produces extremely realistic and detailed Meta Human models and animations, proving their usefulness in both artistic and practical applications. Improvements in accuracy using this type of technology to capture human movement and anatomy, time efficiency in the creation process, and expanded creative possibilities within a smart digital ecosystem are discussed. It demonstrates how access to advanced scanning and motion capture techniques can enhance and optimize the work of 3D artists, and also points out possible directions for future research that can expand digital ecosystems in the creative industries.

articleTitle: Privacy Preservation in IoT: Anonymization Methods and Best Practices
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) offers the most intense technological attempt, allowing objects to collect and exchange vast amounts of information efficiently. While this interconnectivity has various advantages, it also brings severe risks to each individual or organization regarding privacy. As the population of connected devices increases, so does the opportunity to abuse sensitive information, which needs reinforced privacy strategies.
