Risk masking has become one of the most effective strategies for data leaks. This study will examine various anonymization methods, such as homomorphic encryption, data masking, aggregation methods, pseudonymization, and differential privacy, that could be implemented with IoT data. Looking at each method using its performance, pros, and cons offers a comprehensive view of how various methods might be used to protect the user's privacy without compromising the data's utility. In addition to the introduction of multiple methods for anonymization, this study also highlights the privacy preservation methods in IoT environments based on the best practices described. It stresses the importance of determining the value of data, acquiring user acceptance, and following the law, particularly the CCPA and the GDPR. Moreover, it also discusses the importance of building initial privacy in the industry guided by businesses, developers, and users who are shaping the privacy industry’s initial norms. Given the problem and solution for ensuring privacy in IoT, this study aims to provide theoretical depth with some practical examples. Powerful anonymization practices can help stakeholders gain more trust from users, increasing the ethical expansion of IoT (in a privacy-focused direction) and good business practices.

articleTitle: Phishing Detection Dataset: Feature Engineering and Selection
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The Internet has become an inevitable part of our lives. According the statistics two-thirds of the total world’s population is on Internet today. In recent decades, some unpredicted situations, such as COVID-19, have led to an increase usage of Internet services, not only for entertainment and work, but also for education and commerce. Many people have started blindly trusting and sharing personal information and credentials. This opens a bottleneck in the network security. Networks threats and attacks have been around for as long as networks have existed, and they evolve with the network progression. For this reason, the defense of network resources, critical data and personal information have to be addressed and constantly updated in order to face the modern attacks. In this paper authors address sophisticated network attacks, which are based on machine learning (ML) techniques and artificial intelligence. The fight against network offense based on ML and AI require an adequate response which utilize the same technologies. Developing defense mechanisms by using ML approach can provide more robust and effective protection against these complex and dynamically evolving threats. On this way attack can be predicted and thus prevented in real-time using the same techniques attackers employ. This paper focus on phishing detection and defense, based on machine learning. The success of any ML models is strongly dictated by the input data pass through the model during training. Therefore, an enhanced dataset for ML model construction is proposed.

articleTitle: Ergonomic Practices and Occupational Health in Industry 4.0: a Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Although Industry 4.0 has brought about great technological advances and development opportunities, it is not without risks for the safety and health of workers. Automation and the interconnection of systems, while optimizing processes, can generate new, unanticipated ergonomic problems. Repetitive movements, forced postures, and increased cognitive load are some examples. Given this scenario, there is a need to adapt ergonomic practices to this new work environment. This systematic review explores what ergonomic practice optimization strategies exist to ensure the safe and efficient utilization of new technologies under Industry 4.0. Researching and understanding how ergonomic risks evolve in Industry 4.0 is fundamental to designing effective prevention strategies. Methodologies such as the LEST Method, the SOFT Model, and systematic literature reviews can provide a holistic view of the impacts at work. It is key to combine qualitative and quantitative, longitudinal and cross-sectional, participatory and experimental approaches to gain a deep understanding of the transformations of work in the digital age. Only in this way can we ensure the safe and efficient exploitation of new technologies in Industry 4.0, protecting the health and well-being of workers.

articleTitle: State of the Art and Innovations needed for Direct Radiating Arrays to place Very High Throughput Satellite Communications into Technology Reach
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The current work provides the roadmap towards the advent of Very High Throughput Satellite Communications. The key enabler will be the envisioned and presented in detail placement of the Direct Radiating Arrays vision into the reach of the technology. Such an endeavor entails the proper choice of the multi-element electrically large array’s geometry as well as the choice on the element radiator. Those choices should support and implement the overlapping concept in hardware. At the same time, they should leave room for advanced array synthesis techniques to unfold their full potential. Those issues are treated in detail, and proper emphasis is given both on the state of the art as well as to the innovations needed to increase the current relative technological readiness level.

articleTitle: The Role of AI for Smart Environments based on Big Data and IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The modern business environment is characterized by a high degree of variability, uncertainty, and complexity. To cope with the challenges of the environment, to take advantage of new opportunities and to function effectively, organizations rely on innovative techniques, approaches, and models. In this study, based on a semi-systematic literature review method, the entry of AI into the systems based on Internet of Things (IoT) and Big Data and the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) for the construction of the so-called smart environment were investigated. The intelligent environment, from the point of view of business, is an ecosystem that integrates various leading technologies to organize and maintain efficient and highly effective operational structures. AI transforms the data-driven business intelligent environment into an environment that is not only informed and intelligent but is also capable of real-time optimization. I.e., AI transforms traditional business systems into dynamic and highly adaptive systems that can respond to changing conditions in real time. The report explores AI's role as an engine for business with a focus on new opportunities and challenges in its use. The report highlights the critical role of AI in optimizing business intelligent environment to smart environment by leveraging Big Data and IoT. It highlights how new AI driven operations and new insights are improving automation, decision-making, and overall efficiency, modeling intelligent systems that adapt in real-time. These systems subsequently transform industries and improve people's quality of life.

articleTitle: Increasing Student Motivation in Engineering Bachelor and Master Programes through Problem-Based Learning for Sustainable Development Goals
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The article discusses the sociological research conducted at universities in Kazakhstan and Bulgaria. The study aims to analyze the awareness of students and teachers regarding the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) to develop science-based recommendations for integrating sustainable development modules into university curriculum. The research focused on assessing awareness, perception, and understanding of the SDGs, as well as evaluating the integration of sustainable development modules by teachers. For data processed were used IBM SPSS Statistics 27. The authors developed recommendations for universities to include integrating SDGs into curriculum, promoting interdisciplinary research, supporting sustainable technologies, fostering inclusive education, and forming international partnerships. By implementing these strategies, universities can enhance their role in national and global sustainable development, while also strengthening their international reputation.

articleTitle: Blockchain Architectures for Dynamic Quality Pricing in Commodity Trading: A Comparative Study of DAML/Canton and Hyperledger Fabric
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This paper comparatively analyzes DAML/Canton and Hyperledger Fabric blockchain platforms in implementing dynamic quality-based pricing for commodity forward contracts. We developed a mathematical model for quality-based pricing in grain trading and implement it on both platforms. Our analysis covers architectural differences, smart contract development, deployment processes, and performance characteristics, revealing trade-offs in developer experience, transaction transparency, and scalability approaches. The key findings indicate that DAML/Canton offers advantages in expressing complex financial logic and provides fine-grained privacy controls at the contract level, while Hyperledger Fabric provides greater flexibility and potential for higher transaction throughput in certain scenarios, with robust privacy features through its channel-based approach.

articleTitle: Comparative and Predictive Analysis of Kazakhstan’s Sectoral International Trade
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: International trade is one of the main aspects of the global economy, which consists of imports and exports. The study presents sectoral analysis of Kazakhstan's trade for the 2011-2021 period, where provided comparative analysis to explore current dynamics, to reveal insights and predictive analysis to make forecasts and understand the future trend. Accordingly, these types of experiment give efforts aimed at analysis and statistics of our country, as well as at diversifying the current state. In the research comparative analysis provided with the help of visualization and statistical analysis, predictive analysis by means of following machine learning models, Linear Regression, Decision Trees, Random Forests, Gradient boosting, Support Vector Regression. In research estimated the use of production and import resources in 8 sectors, mainly in the manufacturing industry. The results show that the highest export requirements are imposed in certain sectors such as mineral products, fuel and energy products, metals and products made from them. Along with the result of the machine learning models' performance and prediction for the next three year.

articleTitle: Clustering Embroidery Images: A Comprehensive Analysis of Methods to Track the Road of Embroidery Spread
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The paper will reveal how contemporary technologies, like machine learning could help in determining how the embroideries found in traditional Bulgarian clothing are spread among ethnographic regions in the time. The Bulgarian embroidery also known as "shevitsi" is deeply rooted in the country’s cultural heritage. Different regions of Bulgaria have their own distinct embroidery styles, reflecting local traditions, influences, and histories. Tracing these patterns helps in documenting and preserving this regional diversity, which is crucial form maintain the cultural richness of the country. In the paper we have investigating different unsupervised machine learning techniques to cluster images in the dataset based on common features such as colors, motifs, patterns, etc. The paper presents a comprehensive workflow for analyzing Bulgarian embroidery traditions as found in folklore clothing. The analysis suggests that the presence of detail metadata with georeferencing and data annotation, would significantly enhances the ability to trace the spread and evaluation of embroidery motifs. This dataset would allow for a thorough temporal analysis, enabling us to observe how motifs and colors have evolved over time.

articleTitle: Enhancing E-commerce with Artificial Intelligence Applications for Better Customer Experience
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Considering the explosive growth of the fields of science and the industrial community, the use of artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming increasingly frequent, and its advancement has an important influence on both work and life. Throughout the realm of e-commerce, artificial intelligence was additionally successfully utilized and produced positive outcomes, so the technology has emerged as a key driver of ecommerce growth. This paper basically outlines the potential of AI innovation, examines the state of artificial intelligence application in the sector of e-commerce, and primarily examines and analyzes thoroughly from the perspective of AI assistants, intelligent shipping, recommendation generators, and optimal pricing utilization through the analysis of an e-commerce intelligent functioning instance, and probes into its significant effect and major importance. At last, a conventional model for AI acceptance in e-commerce is proposed and improved.

articleTitle: IoT-Enhanced Recycling: A Smart Low-Cost Solution for Sustainable Plastic Waste Management
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This research introduces an innovative Reverse Vending Machine (RVM) system, powered by advanced image processing and deep learning, to revolutionize plastic waste collection and sustainable waste management. Efficiently sorting recyclable plastic bottles, the system, powered by a robust chassis and a low-power Raspberry Pi-based central processing unit, is enhanced by a Firebase-driven image classification model. A user-friendly interface promotes easy interaction, while a companion mobile app introduces a rewarding recycling incentive system. Users accumulate points, which can be redeemed, promoting increased engagement and responsible waste management. With an impressive 82% accuracy rate, low cost, light weight, and ease of use, this RVM system represents a significant advancement in sustainable waste management, offering the potential for substantial environmental impact reduction and contributing to a more sustainable future.

articleTitle: Wireless Communication System with High Data Flow using an ESP32-Based Interface
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This paper proposes a bidirectional communication system designed to handle fast wireless data exchange between an active sensor (AS) based on the ESP32 and an application installed on a personal computer (PC). The data flow is increased by using an additional ESP32 as a computer interface (CI), which is connected to the PC via a USB cable. Data exchange between the ESP32 devices is achieved using the ESP-NOW protocol, developed by the Espressif team. This protocol allows for fast interconnection and data streaming, with the created Wi-Fi network being invisible to other devices. First, the data flow was tested using an MPU6050 sensor, the ESP32’s analog-to-digital converter, and internally generated data, in order to differentiate the data flow based on the source of data acquisition. Second, a UAV arm was simulated. The AS sends MPU6050 sensor data to the PC via the CI, and the PC processes the data and responds with a PWM value to adjust the arm's position to a specific angle. Tests revealed that an increased data flow enables accurate control without the need for complex control techniques. Additionally, the system can be useful in other applications requiring fast wireless data exchange for process control, particularly in research environments. The only requirement for the PC software is to support a serial connection via USB.

articleTitle: The Impact of the Underwater Environment Salinity during the Inspections Carried out with EPS Vision 1712 in Black Sea
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Underwater visibility is significantly impacted by the light and the aquatic environment, particularly salinity. This study explores the propagation of electromagnetic waves, specifically light, through varying salinity conditions, and focuses on the challenges posed by the Black Sea. By employing advanced software simulations, we analyze the attenuation and scattering of light across a range of salinity levels characteristic of the Black Sea. Our findings reveal a strong correlation between salinity and light propagation, with specific wavelengths demonstrating superior penetration and reduced scattering. While our current research utilizes the EPS Vision 1712, a system limited to intensity adjustments, our simulations underscore the potential of wavelength optimization for enhancing underwater image quality. This research contributes to a deeper understanding of light-water interactions in saline environments and provides a foundation for developing advanced imaging technologies for maritime applications.

articleTitle: Securing the Future of Digital Manufacturing: A Review of Vulnerabilities and Mitigation Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This endeavor serves as a systematic review of cyber threats endangering Industry 4.0, specifically addressing Digital Manufacturing (DM) process security. The evolution of the digital industry consequently implies the introduction of new cybersecurity threats that would cause data breaches and intellectual property theft. The paper contributes to the field by analyzing specific real-world scenarios to address cybersecurity vulnerabilities, best practices, adequate cyber standards, and effective mitigation strategies that allow a manufacturing firm to cope with current cyber threats. The research investigations emphasize that workforce cyber knowledge, attentiveness, and whistle-blowing confidence are pivotal in securing the manufacturing environment, thus calling for intensified employee training. Presenting real-world industry case studies provides insight for researchers to conduct future work on enhanced cyber frameworks and mitigation strategies utilizing ML, AI, blockchain, and complex encryption.

articleTitle: Implementation of Intelligent Transport System - An Effective Approach for the Shortage of Workforce in the Transport Sector in the Republic of Croatia
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: For several years now, the Republic of Croatia has been facing a major labour shortage in the transport sector, be it passenger or cargo transport. With the advent of the economic crisis, professional drivers went to the countries of Western Europe in search of better working conditions and better position in society. It is clear that company owners in the Republic of Croatia are not in place to offer as good working conditions as drivers have in Western Europe, so the question remains how to solve this burning problem, since the interest of young people also is decreasing year by year. This research paper will try to get a better insight into the core of the problem, as well as their possible solutions through interviews with five bus drivers, five truck drivers, five owners of truck transport companies and five owners of bus transport companies.

articleTitle: Attitudes on Human Factors in SMEs IT Companies in the Republic of Bulgaria since the Introduction of Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The publication deals with a current problem related to the attitudes on human factors since the introduction of Artificial Intelligence (AI), through a survey among software engineers in small and medium – sized (SMEs) IT companies in the Republic of Bulgaria. This brings to the fore not only the functionality of AI tools and their application in software design, but also the perception of developers towards the tasks of writing, implementing and fixing code. The research was conducted on the territory of three large cities in the Republic of Bulgaria, and a quantitative approach was used in the development of an online survey, through which empirical data was generated in the business of SMEs IT companies. Based on the results, an analysis of the attitudes of the respondents in relation to the use of AI in the software activities of the surveyed companies was made. A smooth but steady trend of a positive human factors attitude towards AI-assisted software design was found. On this basis, a relatively good attitude of developers towards the benefits and advantages of adapting AI to software developments was found.

articleTitle: Image-Based Oil Spill Detection using Deep Learning Techniques: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Oil spills represent a significant danger to marine ecosystems, leading to considerable environmental disasters that adversely affect biodiversity. These incidents, whether accidental or intentional, introduce harmful petroleum hydrocarbons into water bodies, endangering marine life. Various techniques have been developed for oil spill detection, including classification, zone segmentation, threshold segmentation, and edge detection. Recently, deep learning (DL) and machine learning (ML) have shown a lot of potential for successfully detecting and tracking oil spills. This research provides a valuable review of AI-based methodologies for oil spill detection from 2020 to 2024, emphasizing the use of satellite imagery, aerial photographs, and drone imagery for extensive monitoring of marine and coastal areas. The review also discusses the advantages and limitations of these approaches and suggests future directions to improve oil spill detection systems. Ultimately, this article serves as a valuable guideline for researchers providing innovative solutions to mitigate oil spill impacts, aiding in better environmental management and policy development.

articleTitle: Cybersecurity and Autonomous Driving: Experiments with LiDAR Sensor Spoofing
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This research investigates the vulnerability of onboard navigation sensors in autonomous vehicles to cybersecurity attacks. By exploiting the interconnectedness of these systems, adversaries can manipulate sensor data, compromise software, or physically interfere with sensors, potentially leading to serious consequences. This study describes cybersecurity experiments on a hardware-in-the-loop autonomous vehicle testbed, focusing on cyberattacks against LiDAR-based navigation, exploring various attack vectors, including jamming and various methods of spoofing. Experimental results demonstrate the feasibility of these attacks and highlight the need for robust security measures to protect autonomous vehicles from cyber threats. The findings emphasize the importance of ongoing research in developing effective countermeasures to ensure the safety and reliability of autonomous driving systems.

articleTitle: Benefits of using ICT Tools in Higher Education Institutions in Albania
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Information and Communication Technology (ICT) has become an indispensable component of higher education institutions (HEI), revolutionizing the way education is delivered, managed, and accessed. In this digital age, ICT facilitates enhanced learning and teaching through online courses, interactive platforms, and personalized learning experiences. Moreover, ICT empowers research and innovation by providing access to research tools, fostering global collaboration, and aiding data analysis. It enhances communication and collaboration among students, faculty, and staff. This paper offers a comprehensive study of ICT tools applicable in education, focusing on their role and benefits in HEI. It also examines the current situation of public universities in Albania concerning the implementation of these tools. It highlights the challenges faced by Albanian universities in leveraging technology to enhance teaching, learning, and administrative processes, and propose some digital platforms for overcoming these challenges. This paper presents a noble contribution to understanding the importance of ICT tools in managing and increasing the quality of higher education. It also provides an overview of the current state of public HEIs in Albania in relation to the use of ICT tools, addressing some recommendations to overcome the gaps they face.

articleTitle: Academic Certificate Verification: A Practical Comparison between Centralized and Blockchain-Based Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Digitizing the internal services of higher education institutions (HEIs) for generating and verifying academic credentials is crucial for society, as it helps prevent the misuse of diplomas. Although many solutions have been proposed, there is still no unified platform that addresses the limitations of HEIs’ outdated systems. Blockchain technology is often seen as an ideal solution for this purpose, but practical applications are challenging to implement. This article outlines the key features of the DIAR prototype system, a blockchain-based solution for diploma generation and verification, and compares it with other solutions from state-of-the-art. The DIAR system offers a potential solution with its blockchain-based, multi-level secure architecture that emphasizes immutability, identity preservation, traceability, and cryptographic mechanisms. Further, we evaluate and compare the implementation of DIAR and centralized systems.

articleTitle: Effective Energy Management Strategies Evaluation for Small Hybrid Fuel Cell Powered Vessels
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Hybrid fuel cell power systems have demonstrated their ability to lower fuel consumption and enhance transportation performance. However, efficient power transfer between the energy storage system (ESS) and fuel cell is crucial. This study explores the comparative performance of three energy management strategies –optimization-based, rule-based and control-based- for a hydrogen-powered small vessel. The focus is on optimizing fuel efficiency, specifically hydrogen consumption, under river-trip operating conditions. According to simulation results, the most effective energy management method for lowering fuel usage is that relied on control mechanisms. This method’s real-time adaptive control, which efficiently balances fuel cell and ESS utilization, accounts for its superior performance.

articleTitle: Contrast-Enhanced Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Image Based on Enhanced Deep Residual Networks Modified
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Contrast is very important in analyzing medical images, and some contrast enhances the methods that could be very helpful when the image contrast is not good. The enhancement of Deep Super-Resolution (EDSR) is the deep learning (DL) technique that improves the quality and resolution of low-resolution images. Within this study, a transfer learning method grounded in a convolutional neural network (EDSR-Modified) is leveraged for enhancing contrast in cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR). The study conducts experiments at the S7 ISP and ACDC datasets, utilizing the S7 ISP dataset for training and the ACDC dataset for testing the assessment enhancement. This study aims to combine EDSR-Modified with transfer learning to improve CMR image quality, which is used to diagnose cardiovascular diseases. Qualitative comparisons are performed using mean squared error (MSE), peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), and SSIM evaluation metrics. It is observed that the proposed technique outperforms the other techniques.

articleTitle: Improving Data Quality Completeness using Deep Neural Network (DNN) Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Data quality serves as an indicator for transforming information into high-quality outputs. This indicator varies, and the Data Management Association (DAMA) has identified six primary factors, including completeness. Completeness relates to missing values, which are a common issue in time series data. This study proposes addressing the missing value and unknown value problems using Deep Neural Networks, specifically Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs). While RNNs possess the capability to retain information, they are susceptible to the vanishing gradient problem. This challenge is mitigated through the introduction of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks and Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs), both of which demonstrate lower mean square error, indicating superior prediction and imputation accuracy compared to the mean imputation strategy.

articleTitle: Technical Assessment of Green Hydrogen Production in Anion Exchange Membrane Electrolyzers Integrated with Off-grid Renewable Energy Systems at Different Scales
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This study investigates a scalable, off-grid, renewable energy system that uses anion exchange membrane hydrogen electrolyzers to produce hydrogen. The integrated components are a photovoltaic installation, a battery, a hydrogen electrolyzer, intermediate tanks to store the hydrogen that is transferred from the electrolyzer, and two stages of high-pressure compressors, which are used to boost hydrogen pressure in the composite tanks. Based on experimental and technical analysis, it was found that a scalable anion exchange electrolyzer integrated with the pneumatic high-pressure hydrogen compressor can be used as a way to develop seasonal hydrogen storage. An analysis of the impact of electricity needs for hydrogen production and hydrogen compression is also provided.

articleTitle: Precision Agriculture System as a Part of Large Chemical Enterprise Business Model
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Precision fertilization and irrigation systems (as a part of Precision Agriculture Systems) represent an innovation in modern agriculture aimed at optimizing resources and increasing the efficiency of agricultural practices. They use advanced technologies such as sensors, GPS, and software algorithms to provide accurate data and automated solutions for water and fertilizer management. This topic is crucial as it facilitates substantial reductions in resource losses and enhances resource losses and improves yields, consequently reducing the environmental impact of agriculture. A factory business model focused on producing ammonium and phosphorus fertilizers, integrated with consulting services for precision fertilization and irrigation, is highly relevant in today's agricultural industry. This report presents some findings in this direction. Real tests have been done in small pilot farms. Some of the results are given regarding the effectiveness of the precision fertilization and watering system application as a consulting service from the business model of a large chemical enterprise.

articleTitle: Classification of Skin Lesions using PyQt5 and Deep Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This study presents the OncoScan system designed to assist dermatologists in classifying skin diseases using an improved DenseNet121 model. The system was tested on the large HAM10000 dataset of over 10,000 images of skin lesions in seven categories. The DenseNet121 model, characterized by dense connectivity and transient layers, was compared with the InceptionV3 and EfficientNetB7 models. The results demonstrated the superiority of the DenseNet121 model, with an accuracy of 86.04% and an AUC of 96.32%. The OncoScan interface, developed using PyQt5, supports multilingual functionality including English, Russian, and Kazakh, and offers image processing tools. The system's ability to handle image processing and classification with ease makes it a valuable asset for dermatologic diagnostics.

articleTitle: Development of a UVM-Based Verification IP for DO-254 Compliant ARINC429 HDL Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: ARINC429 is a widely adopted data transfer standard in avionics, ensuring reliable communication between critical onboard systems. As aircraft increasingly rely on complex electronics, compliance with safety standards such as DO-254 becomes essential for certifying airborne hardware. The verification of ARINC429 IP cores is crucial to meet these stringent safety requirements. Traditionally, ARINC429 IP cores in the literature have been verified using basic testbenches, which pose challenges in terms of flexibility, time, and cost. This paper introduces a UVM-based verification IP for DO-254 compliant ARINC429 HDL modules, addressing the limitations of conventional verification methods by enhancing test coverage and reducing development time. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study in the literature that uses a VIP to verify an ARINC429 IP core for multiple test scenarios. The VIP offers a reusable, scalable, and efficient verification framework, serving as a robust alternative to traditional loopback-based approaches. It enables thorough validation of ARINC429 IP cores in complex avionics systems. The SIEMENS QuestaSim 10.7a simulator tool is used to extensively test an ASELSAN developed DO-254 compliant ARINC429 IP with the proposed VIP. The results indicate a branch coverage of 91.74%, a statement coverage of 98.34%, and an FEC expression coverage of 96.76%, with an overall average of 95.61%

articleTitle: CNN and SVM Architecture for Face Identification in Multi-View Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Identification is an important part of biometric systems. However, when the system works in real-time, additional problems like pose variation or different scale of the head could occur. These adverse conditions decrease the recognition rate and could fail the identification of a person. Multi-view systems could solve this problem. Nevertheless, it is a challenge to calculate the relative position of the sensors and synchronize the system. We implemented an identification algorithm for multi-view systems that recognize individuals with different head poses. A combination of CNN and SVM was implemented for the task. Various configurations of the CNN and SVM were tested. The network was trained and evaluated on the CroppedYale B dataset and our own dataset, generated by Kinect. A recognition accuracy of 94.71% was achieved with SVM’s RBF kernel for CroppedYale and 99.87% with SVM’s linear kernel for our dataset.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Model Predictive Control for an Electrohydraulic Servo System Using Orthonormal Functions
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The paper presents the implementation of a Continuous-Time Model Predictive Control (CMPC) regulator for controlling an electrohydraulic servo system. The control object is a test bench consisting of three modules and a PC-based data acquisition and control system. The system is modeled in state-space form, accounting for parametric uncertainties. The synthesis of the model predictive controller is performed by approximating the control signal using Laguerre orthonormal functions. The article includes mathematical formulas and relationships that illustrate the modeling approach. Simulations and robust analysis of the closed-loop system are conducted. Through a real-time control system, experimental data and graphs are obtained, demonstrating the performance and optimality of the synthesized control strategy.

articleTitle: Mathematical Modeling of a Mobile Robot's Motion Control System based on LQR
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Now, the development of mobile robots is a promising industry, as these types of robots are acquiring more and more functionality for solving various tasks and in most cases are developed as universal robots that help perform different tasks simultaneously. In this regard, this article discusses the problem of developing a mathematical model of a motion control system for a helicopter-type mobile robot. A mathematical model of a mobile robot motion control system has been developed, using an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) as an example, which allows you to track the flight movement in state space. Simulation model of UAV control system based on a PD-controller has been developed using Matlab/Simulink. The simulation model controls the spatial motion of the UAV through four control channels (roll, pitch, yaw, and altitude). The calculations were performed based on the optimal method using the integral quadratic criterion for a nonstationary linear control system. The simulation results show that the developed mathematical model is an optimal simulation for stabilizing a mobile robot (UAV) in desired positions and orientations.

articleTitle: Collaborative Detection of SQL Injection Attacks using SIEM, Multi-Wazuh Agents, and Diverse Web Application Firewalls
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: SQL injection attacks pose a significant threat to web applications and database systems. This study evaluates the effectiveness of integrating Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) with multi-Wazuh agents and diverse Web Application Firewalls (WAF) to detect threats collaboratively SQL injection attacks. The system was designed using two web servers, each protected by a different WAF—ModSecurity and NAXSI—and a centralized SIEM server employing Wazuh. Tests were conducted using various SQL injection techniques, including Time-Based Blind, Error-Based, and Union-Based attacks. The results indicated that ModSecurity proved more effective in detecting and mitigating Time-Based and Error-Based SQL inj ection attacks, while both WAFs performed similarly in handling Union-Based attacks. The Wazuh platform collected and reported attack data efficiently, offering security teams a clear and centralized view of detected threats. This integration demonstrates the feasibility of implementing collaborative threat detection using a SIEM and diverse WAFs to enhance web application security against SQL injection attacks.

articleTitle: Enhancing Healthcare Facility Management through Non-intrusive Occupancy Detection: A Comparative Study of Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Optimizing patient environments in healthcare is crucial for improving care quality and operational efficiency. This study explores the application of machine learning algorithms for non-intrusive room occupancy detection in healthcare settings, which is essential for creating responsive, patient-centered environments. Using sensors to monitor temperature, light, sound, and CO2 levels, we applied Random Forest (RF), k-nearest Neighbors (k-NN), Support Vector Machines (SVM), and Decision Trees (DT) to predict room occupancy. The study focused on evaluating the accuracy and privacy-preserving capabilities of these algorithms. The results demonstrated that RF, k-NN, and DT performed exceptionally well, achieving high precision, recall, and F1 metrics scores, highlighting their potential for error-free occupancy prediction in healthcare environments. In contrast, while typically robust, the SVM algorithm exhibited slight variations in precision for certain classes, underscoring the importance of algorithm-specific considerations in different healthcare settings. Feature importance analysis revealed that light-based sensors and CO2 levels were critical in determining room occupancy, aligning with existing literature emphasizing environmental factors' significance in patient care settings. This study underscores the valuable role of machine learning in enhancing healthcare environments and advocates for the integration of such technologies into healthcare management systems. This integration promises significant improvements in patient care and resource optimization. Future research should focus on examining the impact of these technologies on patient outcomes and healthcare efficiency.

articleTitle: Secure Techniques for Further Linux Mail Server Protection Against Compromised Accounts
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The article describes some verified and working strategies for protecting Linux mail servers against compromised user accounts through a combination of free, practical solutions that enhance cyber resilience and operational efficiency for real-time detection of account abuse. The paper discusses techniques such as user behavior analytics, hybrid threat detection methods, and log analysis using the "pflogsumm" tool. The advantages of these techniques are demonstrated in real situations of small and medium-sized organizations with limited resources, enabling them to automate processes and identify suspicious activity in real time. The proposed approaches show the potential to create robust mail server protection with minimal investment, achieving high adaptability to emerging threats.

articleTitle: Soiling and Dust Deposition on Solar Panels - Technical Review
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Technologies related to the utilization of solar radiation have undergone serious development in the last decades. However, several factors influence the performance of solar modules, independent of the technology used. Environmental parameters such as temperature, relative air humidity, and degree of air pollution could be significant. The purity of the atmospheric air is determined using the so-called Linke turbidity factor (LTF) and is evaluated on a global basis. As a result of several activities, however, including enterprise activities, commercial activities, transport, etc., the concentration of dust particles can increase many times, leading to a more intensive and permanent accumulation of dust on the panels' surface and significantly reducing their efficiency. In the present work, a critical analysis is made of the factors that have a significant impact on the Soiling and Dust deposition on solar panels. As such, outside air temperature, wind speed and direction, relative humidity, concentration of dust in the air, tilt of the panel relative to the horizon, etc. can be specified.

articleTitle: Smart and Advanced Electrical Skills: Identifying Current Gaps and Emerging Trends
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: With the rise of smart buildings, new expertise gaps and security vulnerabilities are emerging, necessitating a comprehensive understanding of their current state and proactive future planning to address these challenges. Such identification is crucial for mapping the pathway towards vocational modernization (keeping up with trends and goal alignment). To assess these gaps, this paper explores the extensive literature that draws on workshops, expert interviews, and research to identify emerging roles and training needs across seven countries: Greece, Spain, Portugal, Italy, North Macedonia, Germany, and the Netherlands. In particular, it examines the validity of its findings in critical areas such as security, privacy, and the integration of smart grids with energy markets. Additionally, the paper highlights future skills gaps emerging from advancements in IoT, automation, and renewable energy technologies. It emphasizes the growing demand for specialized electrical expertise to optimize energy production, integrate monitoring and storage systems, and manage electric vehicle charging and energy communities effectively. In conclusion, the study identifies critical gaps in expertise and training needed to keep up with the rapid evolution of smart building technologies. Emerging trends highlight the demand for interdisciplinary skills, particularly in IoT, automation, and renewable energy. As these fields advance, expertise in cybersecurity, energy management, and smart grid integration will be crucial, emphasizing the need for proactive workforce development and planning. The findings can be used to inform and direct policymakers towards the smooth reexamination of vocational training.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Bulgarian Heating Fuel Market, with Focus on Hydrogen Use
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The aim of the following study is to analyze the preferences of Bulgarian households regarding different types of heating fuels, their awareness of alternative energy sources such as hydrogen, as well as their satisfaction with their current fuel choice. The survey covers 150 respondents from various regions to ensure data representativeness and to explore attitudes in the context of rising energy costs and environmental challenges. The main findings show that firewood and pellets are the most preferred fuels (21% positive ratings), followed by electric heating (20%) and natural gas (19%). Coal is the least preferred (13%) due to environmental restrictions. The study also finds that 86% of households with monthly costs between 100 and 300 BGN (1.96 BGN = 1 EUR) are willing to switch to more environmentally friendly solutions, while those with lower expenses face financial difficulties in making such a transition. Awareness of alternative fuels, such as hydrogen, is high (83%), yet 60% of the informed respondents report increased heating costs, highlighting the need for more cost-effective alternatives. In conclusion, the study emphasizes the importance of information campaigns and educational initiatives to encourage the transition to sustainable energy sources, while also showing that economic barriers and mistrust remain significant obstacles to the introduction of new technologies.

articleTitle: Evaluating Energy Management: A Comparative Analysis of Smart Meter Versus State-of-the-art Measurement Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This paper provides a comparative analysis of a smart meter and a state-of-the-art measurement device for the use in residential Home Energy Management Systems. It evaluates the impact different meters have on Home Energy Management accuracy and effectiveness, emphasizing that standard smart meters deliver their measured values with a bigger time delay compared to state-of-the-art meters. The study explores how these delays in data acquisition affect energy management but also demonstrates through 210 hours of laboratory experiments, that energy management can be efficiently achieved using a smart meter alone, eliminating the need for additional measurement devices to perform effective energy management. The findings offer practical insights for the use of standard digital electrical meters in Home Energy Management applications.

articleTitle: Zero-Trust Architecture for Securing Internet of Things (IoT) Networks: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Zero Trust (ZT) security architecture eliminates implicit confidence and identity verification, improving cybersecurity. Businesses seeking fast and scalable access control reveal standard ZT solutions' flaws. This thorough study covers Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA) for IoT network security. ZTA may tackle issues via identity verification, fine-grained segmentation, and continuous monitoring. This research contributes to developing a comprehensive framework for ZTA tailored for IoT, emphasizes the integration of cutting-edge technologies, and provides practical guidelines for organizations to adopt ZTA effectively, ensuring a robust security posture against evolving threats. The study covers ZT, ZTA concepts, algorithms workflows, security challenges, and solutions for IoT network security.

articleTitle: Graph Neural Networks for Microseismic Event Detection: Focusing on Distributed Acoustic Sensing Data
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Microseismic event detection is paramount for surveilling subsurface activities including hydraulic fracturing, geothermal energy extraction, and evaluating seismic hazards. Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) technology provides high-resolution spatial and temporal datasets, rendering it an indispensable instrument for identifying microseismic events. Nonetheless, the substantial volume of data and the intricate spatiotemporal interrelations inherent in DAS data present considerable obstacles to conventional signal processing techniques. This research presents a novel approach utilizing Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for microseismic event detection in DAS data. By displaying the spatial and temporal relationships between DAS sensing points as graph structures, the GNN identifies the underlying spatiotemporal patterns linked to microseismic events. According to empirical results, the suggested approach outperforms conventional machine learning frameworks, achieving higher detection accuracy and more computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Verification of RISC-V Load and Store Instructions using a Custom Cocotb based Testbench
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The increasing complexity of modern System-on-Chip designs has introduced significant challenges in pre-silicon verification. The RISC-V Instruction Set Architecture has emerged as a pivotal framework in the modern processor design arsenal, allowing for customization of SoC implementations. This paper presents a systematic approach to simulating and testing the ISA Load/Store instructions using a custom Cocotb-based testbench. The framework developed is extensible to other ISA instructions and can be adapted for verifying different processor designs. The testing results demonstrate the core's ability to handle memory operations correctly, which is crucial for the overall performance of any processor. The success of this project demonstrates the effectiveness of using Python-based verification tools for open-source hardware projects, making them more accessible to a wider range of developers.

articleTitle: A Linear Programming Approach to Carpooling: Enhancing Commute Efficiency at Federal University of Technology Minna
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This study explores the development of a carpooling system specifically designed for the Federal University of Technology Minna staff, utilizing the Civil Engineering Department as a case study. Amidst the escalating concerns of environmental sustainability, traffic congestion, and the economic burdens of individual commuting, carpooling presents itself as a sustainable alternative. Employing a mixed-methods approach, this research integrates a comprehensive survey to assess staff attitudes towards carpooling with the development of a linear programming model aimed at optimizing vehicle routes and allocations. The findings from the survey indicate a significant willingness among the staff to engage in carpooling, motivated by the anticipated benefits such as cost savings and reduced commuting times. The linear programming model further validates the practicality of substantially lowering total travel distances and emissions when compared to solo commuting practices. This targeted investigation showcases the carpooling system's capability not only to enhance commute efficiency among university staff but also positions it as a replicable and sustainable model for other academic institutions. The study contributes valuable insights into the design and operationalization of effective carpooling strategies within the university landscape, proposing a scalable framework applicable to similar urban contexts.

articleTitle: Possibilities to Reduce Consumption of Steel Balls in Drum Mills while Saving Energy Consumption
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: In the present work, an analysis of the main parameters affecting the consumption of steel balls in drum ball mills was made, and research was carried out to obtain a relationship between the ball load and measured values. A passive factorial experiment was carried out on ball mills type 4.5 x 6. The results of the experiment were processed using modern computer programs and are shown tabularly and analytically. Testing of the hardness and chemical composition of the balls used in beneficiation factories processing copper ores, as well as the content of residual iron in the pulp of the used drum ball mills, was carried out. A mathematical model of the ball consumption function was created. A generalized utility function is created while conserving energy consumption. The main parameter in it is the ball filling factor of the mill drum, fully describing the grinding process in drum ball mills. The results of all these activities were analyzed and conclusions were summarized on the basis of which engineering solutions leading to a reduction in the consumption of balls in drum mills were proposed.

articleTitle: Iterative Design Approach of a Ferrite and Aluminium Caging for a WPT System
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This work investigates the change of the key parameters self-inductance, mutual inductance and coupling factor applying a finite element analysis (FEA) with different lateral shielding configurations encircling a WPT system. Specifically, the ferrite and aluminium shielding is iteratively increased laterally until a complete caging around the couplers is created. Furthermore, the magnetic flux density and thus the protection against magnetic radiation for the mentioned configurations is examined in compliance with defined limit values of the ICNIRP (International Commission on Non-Ionizing Radiation Protection) and the IEEE/ICES (International Committee on Electromagnetic Safety). The result of this investigation ultimately provides information about the advantages and disadvantages of a lateral shielding with regard to important WPT key parameters and shielding conditions.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Impact of Artificial Intelligence and Automation in the Postal Services Sector Labour Market
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The Postal services sector is increasingly automating human labour, which is likely to be reduced to the point of redundancy in future. The introduction of Automatic Post Stations (APS) in the Bulgarian postal sector is gaining momentum and is one of the most recent examples of a disruptive innovation in the Bulgarian economy. This study aims to examine and analyse the use cases of artificial intelligence (AI), APS and other digital technologies as a disruptive innovation (closing technology) and their impact on employment in the Postal services sector. It is thematically linked to another study by the authors examining the impact of AI and other disruptive innovations on the business processes in the sector. This study examines APS development statistics in Europe and Bulgaria, as well as potential job losses in the Postal services sector. The transformative impact of automation and AI on employment in the postal and courier services sectors is outlined, highlighting new opportunities, advantages and disadvantages. Conclusions are drawn based on the investigation and analyses.

articleTitle: Investigating the Impact of Data Preprocessing on Brain Tumor Detection using Neural Network Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The present article analyses how data augmentation affects the performance of several deep learning models, including CNN, ResNet, and VGG19. By comparing performance indicators across different augmentation scenarios, this article assesses the effectiveness of augmentation strategies for each model. The results show that data augmentation greatly increased performance for the CNN model enhancing parameters like accuracy, precision etc. At the same time data augmentation had no influence on the ResNet model’s finel results although it showed a positive increasing in the process. Experiments also reveal very minor gains for the VGG19 model. These findings underscore the need of adapting augmentation strategies to each model's unique traits. Future research should concentrate on optimizing and investigating innovative data augmentation techniques to improve model performance and generalization.

articleTitle: Optimal Mitigation of Renewable Energy Curtailment in Greece through Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The limitation of energy curtailment produced through Renewable Energy Sources (RES) is obstructed by technical, economic, and political factors. This reduction has negative financial consequences for renewable energy producers and may lead to higher electricity prices for consumers. To address these challenges, this study aims to explore the potential benefits of hydrogen energy storage as a solution to reduce renewable energy curtailment and improve the economic viability of renewable energy projects participating in the Day-Ahead Market (DAM). Using recent data from the Independent Power Transmission Operator (IPTO) and the Hellenic Energy Exchange (HEnEx), the study implements a metaheuristic optimisation algorithm, the Moth-Flame Optimiser (MFO), to investigate the feasibility of the proposition. The methodology computes a 1.23% return on investment over an eight-month operational period, with minimal monthly participation. By reducing the costs of the purchase and installation of system components, combined with governmental support in the form of incentives, the current obstacles could be removed.
